chapters.title: Chapter 1936 Bittersweet Emotions
paragraphs: Quinlan Elysiar left his women to their war and walked out into the corridor, where the noise of the sickroom followed him through two closed doors.
He had one more woman to see, and she was the only one who had watched the whole thing.
A seam of pale light opened in the corridor at his gesture, and beyond it hung a sky full of stars no navigator on Iskaris had ever charted. He stepped through, and the estate closed behind him.
The soul realm was quiet, as it always was, no wind, the stars low, dense, and motionless overhead.
Pink light pulsed from the tree at the heart of the clearing into roots that curled deep into the dark soil, and up in its branches a small blue shape was swinging its legs.
"He's here!" Mimi called down.
On the throne, the Primordial Demon of Lust had already arranged herself.
Nyxara sat with one leg crossed over the other and her chin on her hand, pink eyes half-lidded, and she had clearly been sitting exactly like that since the moment his knee touched Jasmine's floor.
The crimson brand on her abdomen glowed through the dark.
"My Ruin~" she purred. "Congratulations. Many great men fumble what you just did."
"You watched."

"Of course. I watch everything." She uncrossed her legs and crossed them the other way. "Your little samurai petted you like the most precious thing to have ever existed. I'm happy for you, my love. Truly."
He came up the steps of the throne. For once, she stayed in her chair.
She meant it.

Billions of years of watching men marry had taught the Primordial Demon of Lust exactly what a wedding was worth, and she had ended enough of them from the inside to know the difference between a bargain and the thing he had just done.
Her Ruin had knelt, and she had been proud enough to bite her own knuckle on the throne.
But she was also a woman, and the woman had been alone in the dark for a very long time.

She had decorated this place for him. She had made the sky pretty, painted the child's nails, and kept a dead realm alive so it would feel like home on the days he came here because he needed something.

Tomorrow there would be a hall on a square full of people watching him marry everyone but her. She would watch it from this chair. She would cheer, and she would mean that too, and it would still be the loneliest afternoon of her very long life.
There was nothing to be done about any of it. She was too old for fits, too proud, and far too happy for him to spoil it with her insecurities.
So she smiled, and kept it to herself.
"You shouldn't be here," Nyxara said, and flicked her fingers at the air behind him where the seam had been. "This moment is too precious to waste on me. We can have fun later. Go back to your brid-"
He went down on one knee in front of the throne.
The composure went out of her mid-word.
Nyxara looked at him with her mouth still open on the rest of the sentence.
"...You just said a man kneels once," she managed. "Once in his life. You just said it. Are you not a man?"
"I am a man who breaks the rules when they're to be broken."
"That is not-"
"Especially for you."
He took her hand off the arm of the throne and held it, and she let him, because she had apparently forgotten how her arm worked.
"I wish I could show you off like the rest of them," Quinlan said. "I wish I could walk you into that hall tomorrow and let the whole world see my precious demoness in all her glory."
"You don't come out of this realm for anything smaller than the end of the world, and if you did, nobody on that square would look at a bride again. So I can't."
Her fingers had gone still in his.
"But that doesn't make you any less my woman. It doesn't mean you deserve any less than they do." He looked up at her and smiled, soft and tender, full of love. "So I'm asking you properly."
"Nyxara. Will you be my wife?"
For a long moment, the Primordial Demon of Lust did not do anything at all.
Overhead, the legs stopped swinging.
Then her free hand came up and pressed itself flat over her mouth, and above it her eyes went wide, then wider, then began to shine.
"...Ask me again," she said through her fingers.
"Will you be my wife?"
"Again."
"Nyxara, will you-"
"Yes!" It came out as a squeal, and the demoness who had shattered the will of a relic blade without leaving her chair shot to her feet so fast the throne rocked.
"Yes! Yes, yes, yes, obviously yes!!! How dare you?! How dare you do this to me?! Look at me, I'm shaking!"
She was. Both hands had gone to her cheeks, and she was standing on the top step of her throne, bouncing on her toes.
"Are you sure I deserve-"
"Yes." Quinlan refused to hear the rest of it.
"But I'm-"
"Nyxara. I love you, I want you to be my wife. That's it."
The demoness was out of excuses.
Up in the tree, Mimi had both fists knotted in her own hair and was giggling so hard the branch shook.
"She's crying!" the little dryad announced to the whole realm. "I've never seen her make that face!"
"I am not crying, you little ruffian-"
"It's my turn!" Mimi dropped out of the branches and landed in the grass with a bounce. "You always do my nails, so it's my turn now! I'm doing yours! For the wedding!"

"..." Nyxara merely wept in response. She came down the last step of the throne and threw both arms around the man on his knee, hard enough to take him off it, and buried her face in his neck exactly where she always did when the performance ran out.
He held her. She was shaking against his chest, the brand on her abdomen burning crimson against him, and for once the Primordial Demon of Lust had nothing theatrical to say.
"I love you," she said into his neck. "I love you so much. I love you so much it's stupid. I've had billions of years to learn better and I haven't learned a thing."
"Good."
"I'm going to be a terrible wife."
"I'm counting on it."

"H-how dare you! Deny it! It's your duty as a man!" She laughed, wet, into his collar. She did not let go. Behind them, a small blue dryad was already hunting through the grass for the bottle of pink.
It was time to hold the greatest marriage Iskaris had ever known!

chapters.title: Chapter 1937 The Grand Ceremony
paragraphs: Kaelira's workshop stood behind the main house, in the new shadow of the trunk, and the forge inside it was already lit when Quinlan came through the door.
He had guessed it would be. The shy elf fled to her anvil the way other people fled to bed, and the house behind him was full of screaming brides.
She stood at the bench with her sleeves rolled past the elbow and her dark blue bob tied back, laying out stock in a row.

Pale gold, then silver, then a coil of mithril drawing-wire beside a rod of orichalcum. At the end of the row sat a raw adamantite core the size of her fist, drinking the forge-light and giving nothing back.
The deep metals had come up from the mountain at his word. Brokk, First Hammer of the royal smithy, had emptied the crown's rack onto an elf's bench.
Kaelira did not look up. "How many?"
Quinlan grinned.
"Let's make twelve."
The Runeweaver Titan's hands stopped on the adamantite core.
She counted under her breath, lips moving, one finger tapping the bench for each name.
She reached ten, then added Nyxara without hesitation, and that was eleven. Her hand stopped over the twelfth with nothing left to put under it, and she raised her violet eyes to him.
"Black Fang?"
He only smiled at her.
"Gotta be prepared."
"..." Kaelira looked at him a beat longer, then picked up her tongs. "Twelve," she said, and left it there.
That was the last quiet thing either of them said for two hours.
"Serika's cannot be gold," she told him, already heating the first bar. "Gold softens at her hands. She'll melt it off her own finger the first time she throws a punch. Adamantite is our best bet."
"And Blossom's?"

"Has to survive lightning. Mithril, with a conductive channel through the core so the current has somewhere to go." She turned the bar in the coals. "Vex's needs a groove for a curse. If I don't give her one, she'll carve it herself and ruin everything."
She called metals off the rack and reasons off the top of her head. The shy elf who said yes to doorframes was nowhere in that workshop.
All twelve rings for her best friends had to be perfect.

Ayame's band would carry a water-line that ran the circumference without a seam. Aurora's would be plain silver, the smith said, because Aurora would want to be able to read the script in it. Jasmine's would be gold, the real kind, and Kaelira would cut the seal herself.
*Tang. Tang. Tang.*
His part came last, as it always did.
She did the shaping, the cutting. He came in behind her with the mana and lit what she had made.
Twelve times a script only the two of them had ever written would wake in the metal and settle.
Sometime after the fourth ring, watching her bent over the bench with her ears pinned back in concentration, Quinlan said what he had been thinking since the door.
"You know it's your wedding too. I can do this myself."
"Absolutely not."
"What if I ask for help? Brokk, Rykar, or-"
"No. I want to do it."
"I know, but I'd feel bad if you spent this time working for others. Are you sure this is okay?"
The smith set both hands flat on the bench and looked at them instead of him.
"...They're my family too."
Her palm settled on the cooling adamantite of Serika's ring.
"It makes me happy to do this for them. With every hammer strike, I can imagine their joy as you present them their rings."
She was spending the one day she had on them and calling it a gift to herself.
"I understand."
He kissed the top of her head, once, before she picked up her tongs.
"Also," Kaelira said to the anvil, in a voice about half its usual size, "I'm ready."
"Oh?"
"For tomorrow. I'm ready." She turned a bar in the coals that did not need turning. "I've been ready."
She crossed to the far wall of the workshop before he could ask what that meant, reached up to a rune-stud set into the stone at head height, and pressed it with her thumb.
The wall opened.
It slid back without a sound, and behind it, under lamps that lit themselves, stood a row of dress forms.

She had been sewing her own wedding dress in secret, one attempt at a time.
"Kaelira, how long have these been-"
"No questions."
"Fourteen. You've made fourteen of-"
"No questions!" Her face had gone pink, and she quickly closed the door, hiding the evidence away.
Quinlan's amused laughter lasted for long enough to make her pout three times in a row.

Miri Town had been built as a skeleton, Jasmine liked to say, a frame for a nation to grow into.
In a night and a day the dwarves had put a hall on her square that would have shamed a cathedral.

But they had given it no roof, for Rosie's canopy was the roof. It stood over the whole town, miles up, and where the square lay beneath it the leaves had turned white for the occasion, so that noon came down through them soft as lamplight.
The four races of Iskaris filled the square to its edges and spilled down every street that fed it.
Farmers from the Program in their festival best. Dwarves down from the mountain with their beards oiled and braided.
Elves in white from Elysaria, and along the eastern side a wedge of beastkin with cubs on their shoulders, the four great lords standing at the front of it.
"Is it true he's marrying all of them?!"
"Every one, my cousin's cousin said. At the same time."
"Can you even do that?"
"He conquered the continent. He can do whatever the fuck he wants."
The dwarves had built the front rows a step higher than the rest, and the powers of the continent stood there in a line.
Queen Felicity of Vraven stood first, fourteen and radiant with the importance of it, her father the retired king one step behind her.
Brokk of the royal smithy, beside her in the same formal coat as before, was already sweating in it.
Near the back, dressed for the occasion and standing very straight, was Kaede Fujimori, who had come down from Silverwind with Elder Chizuru at her side.
And in a row of their own, holding papers, sat the heads of the Vesper Consortium.

The old Mediator sat in the middle of them with a folded license on his knee, beaming into his beard. Maelstrom, the Consortium's general, sat at the end of the row looking like he was attending the funeral of his old life.
It was a funeral, in a way.

The Consortium had bled beside the Villain's armies through the war, and Quinlan had thanked them the only way a state could thank a syndicate: he made them official. Recognized, licensed, employed, and paid out of the treasury of the very nation they used to rob.
The price was every trade the Consortium had been built on. No more narcotics, no more slaves, no more ferrying whatever paid through whichever border the crown was not watching.

What they got in exchange was the job they had trained for, seen from the other side. Nobody on Iskaris knew better how a man hid money from a state, moved goods past a checkpoint, or bought a magistrate, because nobody on Iskaris had done more of it.

The Obsidian Circle, the Consortium's heads, were now the best hounds an empire could ask for, and the Mediator looked delighted to be one. He had come away from Quinlan with a snippet of other news: soon, nobility, the hierarchy one gained at birth, would be 'examined'.
That, together with their new position, meant that they were set up to reap immense rewards while the privileged dogs of the old age sank to irrelevance.
Along the aisle that ran from the hall's great doors to the altar, Isveth's shrine maidens stood in two white lines with their hands folded, and Isveth herself stood at the head of them.
Their Holy Son, the First Elf's own child, was marrying his lovers today.
This was a day all elves would celebrate for the rest of their lives.

Arch Priestess Elisabeth, Dawn Breaker, chosen of the Goddess, stepped up to the altar in white and gold vestments that fell straight as scripture. Dawn-colored light gathered on her right hand like the first sun of the day.
Behind her came Arch Priestess Velara of the New Whisperfield cathedral, then the Goddess's church in numbers, two full columns of priestesses in white and gold.
The Goddess's church held the altar because Quinlan had asked it to.
His women knew by now that the Goddess was not the figure in the stories they had been raised on.

But many of them had been little girls once, kneeling at a shrine with their hands folded, wondering whether they would one day have a grand wedding of their own, blessed in white and gold at an altar like this one.

The stakes had changed a hundred times since then, yet the dream had stayed exactly where it was. So the Primordial Villain had gone to her temple and asked for the prim and proper wedding so many of his wives had grown up wanting.
At the altar, the Dawn Breaker raised her lit hand and addressed the square in a voice that was warm and enormous at once.

"People of Iskaris. The temple was asked whether the Goddess would witness this marriage, and the temple carried the question to her altar." She took a deep breath before declaring: "The Goddess answers yes. Let all who stand in this square stand as her witnesses."
The great doors opened.
Quinlan Elysiar came through them with a woman on each arm.

On his right walked Emily, the head maid of his estate, who had run his house since the beginning and was crying before her second step. On his left walked Governor Myrasyn of Elysaria, in the white of her people, with her chin up and her eyes wet.

He had guessed it would be.
The shy elf fled to her anvil the way other people fled to bed, and the house behind him was full of screaming brides.
She stood at the bench with her sleeves rolled past the elbow and her dark blue bob tied back, laying out stock in a row.
Pale gold, then silver, then a coil of mithril drawing-wire beside a rod of orichalcum.

Brokk, First Hammer of the royal smithy, had emptied the crown's rack onto an elf's bench.
Kaelira did not look up.
"How many?"
Quinlan grinned.
"Let's make twelve."
The Runeweaver Titan's hands stopped on the adamantite core.
She counted under her breath, lips moving, one finger tapping the bench for each name.
She reached ten, then added Nyxara without hesitation, and that was eleven.
Her hand stopped over the twelfth with nothing left to put under it, and she raised her violet eyes to him.
"Black Fang?"
He only smiled at her.
"Gotta be prepared."
"..." Kaelira looked at him a beat longer, then picked up her tongs.
"Twelve," she said, and left it there.
That was the last quiet thing either of them said for two hours.
"Serika's cannot be gold," she told him, already heating the first bar.
"Gold softens at her hands.
She'll melt it off her own finger the first time she throws a punch.
Adamantite is our best bet."
"And Blossom's?"
"Has to survive lightning.

"Vex's needs a groove for a curse.
If I don't give her one, she'll carve it herself and ruin everything."
She called metals off the rack and reasons off the top of her head.
The shy elf who said yes to doorframes was nowhere in that workshop.
All twelve rings for her best friends had to be perfect.
Ayame's band would carry a water-line that ran the circumference without a seam.
Aurora's would be plain silver, the smith said, because Aurora would want to be able to read the script in it.
Jasmine's would be gold, the real kind, and Kaelira would cut the seal herself.
*Tang.
Tang.
Tang.*
His part came last, as it always did.
She did the shaping, the cutting.
He came in behind her with the mana and lit what she had made.
Twelve times a script only the two of them had ever written would wake in the metal and settle.
Sometime after the fourth ring, watching her bent over the bench with her ears pinned back in concentration, Quinlan said what he had been thinking since the door.

I can do this myself."
"Absolutely not."
"What if I ask for help?
Brokk, Rykar, or-"
"No.
I want to do it."
"I know, but I'd feel bad if you spent this time working for others.
Are you sure this is okay?"
The smith set both hands flat on the bench and looked at them instead of him.

Her palm settled on the cooling adamantite of Serika's ring.

She was spending the one day she had on them and calling it a gift to herself.
"I understand."
He kissed the top of her head, once, before she picked up her tongs.
"Also," Kaelira said to the anvil, in a voice about half its usual size, "I'm ready."
"Oh?"
"For tomorrow.
I'm ready." She turned a bar in the coals that did not need turning.
"I've been ready."

chapters.title: Chapter 1938 Beautiful Procession
paragraphs: His mothers were away. Myrasyn walked him in Lumi's place, while Emily walked him for Miri and Katalin both, his primordial mother and his human one.
Emily wore a dress instead of a uniform and held her Master's arm as if it might be taken from her.
"Master... the mistresses should be... I am only the... forgive me, I told myself I would not-"
"You've had my house since the beginning," Quinlan said, and put his hand over hers on his arm. "I'd be honored."
"I'll tell her everything when she returns," Myrasyn said on his other arm, so quietly that only he heard it, and held on harder.

They walked him. Down the aisle between two lines of weeping elves, past the heads of the Consortium and the beaming Mediator, past Kaede Fujimori, past four beastkin lords and a queen of fourteen, to the foot of the altar where the Dawn Breaker waited.

Emily let go of his arm one finger at a time, curtsied to the Arch Priestess, and went to the front row, where Anna and Beatrice were waiting to hold her up. Myrasyn bowed to Quinlan, then to the altar, and took her place in the front row beside Felicity.
Then the doors at the far end opened a second time, and the flower girls came through them.

Rosie Elysiar walked in front, solemn as a proclamation, with her hands folded, scattering nothing at all. Overhead, the white canopy did it for her, and petals came down the length of the hall in a slow, steady snow.
Feng Jiai walked one step behind her with a basket, in a formal robe, looking like a younger Ayame who had been told to behave, and threw petals by the handful.
"Rosie is the flower girl," Rosie informed the square, in case anyone had missed it.
"We're the flower girls," Feng corrected through her teeth.
"Rosie is the flower girl. Feng is the helper."
"Like father like daughter, huh?" Feng grumbled, and kept throwing petals. "Always treating me like a sidekick..."

When they reached the altar, Feng dumped what was left of the basket on the steps, dug the ring box out from under the last of the petals, and took the place at the groom's left. Then she informed him, with uncharacteristic softness, "I'm happy for you..."
"Thank you, Feng." Quinlan smiled, and was about to give her a headpat when his arm was slapped away.
"I spent the entire morning on my hair! Don't you dare!" Feng Jiai hissed, and Quinlan grinned.
"My bad. Got carried away."
"Hmph!"
The brides had drawn their order from a hat the night before at Lucille's suggestion. This was the best way to avoid souring the mood.
Ayame was the first to agree, not wanting to go first just because she was the first woman he met or his second-in-command.
The Hexwitch came first, and the square learned what silence sounded like.

Vex wore white with red accents, no horns, exactly as advised. The woman walking her down the aisle was Black Fang, who had put on black, and the aisle got very wide as she came down it. Behind the pair walked Raika and Orianna, Vex's sister-disciples under Black Fang.
"Master, you're walking too fast."
"You are walking too slow."
"It's a procession! People are supposed to look at me!"
"They are looking at you."
At the altar, Black Fang set her disciple's hand in Quinlan's and let go.
"Hubby!!" said Vex, which covered everything else.
Then the Venomborne Terror turned around, and the aisle she had just walked down was empty before anyone saw her leave it.
She was standing at the great doors in the same breath, hands at her sides, waiting for them to open.
Ayame came second.

The samurai walked the aisle in white with her black hair pinned up, glowing brilliantly. On her right arm, in a black coat she had plainly been forced into, was Iris Ravenclaw. On her left... Ayame's eyes widened.
"Big sis?" Ayame gasped. "You ran."
"I did not run."
"For me...?" Ayame beamed like a second sun, and took Black Fang with her left arm. "What a present... Thank you!"
"..." Black Fang merely held her hand tighter.
The Demon of Vengeance walked stiff as a plank and stared straight ahead.
"Walk faster. Everyone's staring."
"You're the one dragging your feet~"
At the foot of the altar Iris put the samurai's hand into Quinlan's as if handing over a sack of grain. "Before I beat her up," she told him. Then she went and found a pillar to lean on.
Black Fang put her sister's other hand into his, held it there for exactly as long as the gesture required, and looked at him once.
Then the Venomborne Terror joined Iris, back against the same pillar, observant.

Vargis Ironfang walked his daughter Kitsara in full war-chief bearing, jaw set, eyes forward, five white tails wrapped around his forearm because the foxkin could not stop them. His sons Darius and Fenrik followed at a respectful distance, mostly to make sure he did not cry in public.
Blossom nearly said yes at the doors.
"Master!!"

Every head in the square turned, and the gorgeous dogkin stood at the far end of the aisle in white with a channel down the back for her tail, ears up, shining with achievement. Her mother Natalie had a hand between those ears, and her elder sister Poppy had the other arm.

"Don't say yes yet, dummy," Poppy hissed into her ear, as low-key as possible, sweating bullets over her little sis making a fool of herself. As a big sister, she took it as her duty to ensure Blossom was as radiant as possible today.
"Only after the question is asked!! Blossom remembers!" Blossom decreed, tail wagging so hard the doors behind her nearly fell off.
"That's right, sweetheart," Natalie said, tears streaming. "I'm so happy..."
Blossom was walked down the aisle by her family, and at the altar she looked up at her Master with her whole heart on her face.
Serika came next, and so did the sound of hydraulics.

Rykar Vael, the unyielding anvil of the Fire Nation, walked his daughter down the aisle on four mechanical limbs that hissed at every step, burn scars up his neck, back straight as it had ever been. He was crying so hard he could barely see the altar.
Seraphiel came in moonlight.

Sylvaris of House Vaelorith walked her daughter in the full silver glory of a moon-elf matriarch, and the light coming off her made the white leaves overhead look dim. Sera, shameless in a dress that had been cut to prove several points at once, kept giggling at her mother.
"Mom, stop glowing so much. You're upstaging me!"
Sylvaris said nothing at all, pressed her lips together, and inclined her head to Quinlan when she gave him her daughter's hand.
Aurora Lorien came with both parents, and one of them was not going to make it.

Naomi walked on her daughter's right, steady as a table. Gideon, on her left, had lost the ability to speak somewhere near the doors. The man who lectured nobles without batting an eye could only look at his girl, wipe his face, and try again.
"My girl-"
That was as far as he got, every time.
"Walk, dear," Naomi told him softly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1939 Yes
paragraphs: Aurora reached the altar with her eyes wet, and said, to the only man she had ever loved, "It's really happening..."
"It was always just a matter of time," Quinlan smiled.
Lucille came with her daughter.

Mavena walked her mother down the aisle with a flat expression and a grip that would have held a horse. Despite being the only one in the harem who had been married before, Lucille looked just as stiff as the others.
"Hold me before I faint," she whispered to Mavena.
"Mom... You should already be-"
"I just signed some papers back then to save my life. This is very different!"
Kaelira came in the fourteenth dress.

There had been thirteen before it, and nobody in the square would ever know. White silk, cut close, no train. Her teammates Liora and Shallan walked her, one on each arm, a friend to each side. The Runeweaver Titan went scarlet to the ears at the first step but did not stop walking.
Jasmine came last, because it was her square. She had asked for it instead of drawing from the hat.
Gina Argentis walked her daughter down it, squealing under her breath the entire way, and the Tyrant of Commerce wore a long column of pale gold with her seal embroidered at the sternum.
Her eyes flickered once, blue to gold and back, as she passed the Obsidian Circle Members with their licenses.
Just like that, all the otherworldly, beautiful brides stood in a line at the foot of an altar.
The Dawn Breaker raised her lit hand over all of them.

"Quinlan Elysiar," called the Arch Priestess. "Before the Goddess, and before the four races of this realm assembled, do you take these women as your wives, to keep and to honor for as long as the Goddess grants you days?"
He looked down the line, every face, and it took a while.
"I do."
"And you, each in your turn, standing before the same Goddess and the same realm: do you take this man as your husband?"
"Yes," said Ayame, eyes fondly on Quinlan.
"Yes!" Vex wasted no time responding, pentagram eyes flaring.
"Yes~" Kitsara purred, tails up.
"Yes!!!" Blossom shouted.
"Yes!" Serika's hair flared.
"Yes," said Sera, delicate hands on her chest.
"Yes..." cried Aurora, wiping her tears.
"Yes~" Lucille sang.
"...Yes," said Kaelira, and for once, she gazed deep into Quinlan's eyes while speaking.
"Yes," finished the Tyrant of Commerce.
Feng held out the box, and Quinlan put Kaelira's rings on ten hands.
Each metal had been chosen for the hand it went onto. Each band woke as it settled, the script the two of them had written into it lighting once under the skin and going quiet.
Kaelira watched every single one go on, and by the time he reached her own, she had both hands over her mouth.
Then he turned to the empty air beside the altar.
A seam of pale light opened at the flick of his pointer finger, and through it hung a sky full of stars.
Nyxara was already standing at the edge of his soul realm, on her side of the threshold, where he always opened the gate. The Primordial Demon of Lust could not leave that place.
But the man who had knelt to her only yesterday stepped into the seam to the waist, took her hand, and slid an orichalcum ring onto it.
Her arm trembled the entire time he held it.
"Nyxara," he said, low, for her alone. "Do you take me?"
She looked at the ring on her hand, then at him, and this time the demoness answered on the first asking.
"I do, my Ruin."
Quinlan left the seam open.
"Then, in the sight of the Goddess, you may kiss your brides," decreed the Dawn Breaker.
He kissed them, one at a time, down the line.
Ayame tiptoed. But that wasn't enough to close the gap, so she pulled his head down to hers and held it there a beat past the kiss, with nothing in her face but tenderness.
Vex bit him. Kitsara used her tongue with far too much enthusiasm in front of ten thousand people and her father.
Blossom's went on too long.
"Too long, sweetheart," Natalie whispered from the front row.
"Ah!! Blossom can't think straight when Master is kissing her!!" the dogkin cried, and through immense willpower pulled back.
Then she went back for a quick kiss before using both hands to hide her lips, chiding herself.
Serika laughed at the adorable sight and got tears on his collar.
Sera made hers a real spectacle, moving with practiced motions of perfect elven grace.
Aurora closed her eyes and held onto his lapels.
Lucille kissed him slow, in front of every witness she had ever wanted.
Kaelira shut her eyes, went scarlet to the shoulders, and did not surrender a centimeter.
Jasmine rose onto her toes to give his hand better purchase on her waist.
"You're modest for once, hmm?" she purred, referring to how Quinlan had a tendency to grab a handful of her buttocks while kissing her in public.
"Just this once," Quinlan winked.

Then he went back to the seam, took Nyxara by the waist through the pale light, and kissed her on her side of the threshold. She held his face, and the brand on her abdomen burned a brilliant pink through her silk.
"By the grace of the Goddess and the office she laid upon me, I, Elisabeth Valorian, Dawn Breaker, proclaim you husband and wives, from this day forward, in her light."
The square broke.
Dwarves roared from the far side and beat their chests until their braids came loose. The elves along the aisle were weeping in two neat lines, Isveth on her knees at the head of them.
Emily, held upright between Anna and Beatrice, had given up entirely. Gideon Lorien had found his voice and was using it to sob.
His women stood in a row at the front of it all, ringed, kissed, and crying, holding onto each other, and for once, none of them had anything clever to say.
Quinlan let it run.
He stood under the white canopy with ten wives in a row and an eleventh watching from a door into the stars, and let ten thousand people be as loud as they liked for as long as they liked.
Then he raised one hand, and the square went still to the last cub.
"Not long ago, the elves knelt to me. Then the humans, then the dwarves, and yesterday the beastkin. The Continent of Iskaris is now united under a single banner, for the first time in its history."
He looked at Jasmine when he said the next part, and the Tyrant of Commerce had gone very still.
"I never gave our nation a name, because it wasn't yet time. Now it is."
He turned back to the square.
"This land is the Empire of Iskaris. Its capital is Miri Town. Its laws are the ones its governor writes."
"And these women," he said, and his voice dropped, "are its empresses."
The roar this time built, and kept building, ten thousand voices finding one name to throw at the sky.
In the middle of it the governor of Miri Town stood with both hands over her seal and her eyes gone gold, mouthing the words to herself.
The Empire of Iskaris.
Quinlan looked up.

The last of his daughter's blessing was running out over the white canopy, minutes of it now, and the window that had opened for him at the beastkin fire had told him plainly what he could do with it.
The Suppression stood until the sovereign willed it broken.
Quinlan willed it.
Overhead, the sky showed its wall.
Nobody on Iskaris had ever seen it. It had been there since before any of their grandparents' grandparents, invisible.
Now it stood over the whole continent in plain sight: a vast pane laid across the sky from horizon to horizon, catching the noon light with a dull, greasy sheen.
Millions of faces turned at once, all over the continent.
"What is that?!"
"The Restriction. That's the Heavenly Restriction, that's-"
"It's real. It's really up there!"
"At long last..." Against her pillar, Black Fang had lifted her gaze to the wall that had forcibly stopped her progression, her eyes swirling with pure, unfiltered mania.
Her swirling eyes lit up as she whispered:
"Begone."
The crack started directly above Miri Town.

It ran outward from that point in every direction, a white line racing across the pane faster than any eye could follow, branching as it went, until the whole sky over Iskaris was a web of fractures with the Villain's square at its center.
*KRRRRK-*
Then it came down like glass.

Millions of people flinched under a sky falling in pieces, shards the size of provinces turning over as they fell, thinning to clear and gone before they ever reached the canopy. Beyond them, where the wall had been, was nothing but open blue.
They were free.
The vast world of Thalorind lay open to the denizens of Iskaris, birds in a gilded cage no longer.
"Now then," the Primordial Villain said to the open sky, with ten empresses holding onto him.
"It's time to explore."
Author: The novel's 13th arc, 'Consolidation of Power' is over. This point also marks the proper end of the Iskaris Saga.

When I sat down more than two years ago, bored out of my mind, never would I have thought that the little passion project I started writing would change my life so profoundly. I'm forever grateful for all the support you've shown over the novel's many chapters.
Now, it's time to look outward, to the great unknown that is the world of Thalorind.
The Primordial Villain's journey is only just getting started.
PS: I might need some time off to plan out what's to come. We'll see.

chapters.title: Chapter 1940 Sovereign Powers
paragraphs: Quinlan Elysiar stood at the altar in Miri Town's square with ten empresses holding onto him and a sky coming down in pieces over all of them.
The shards of the Heavenly Restriction were still falling.
Panes the size of provinces turned over in the noon light, thinned to clear, and were gone before they ever reached his daughter's white canopy. Beyond them the blue went on forever.

The square was screaming. Ten thousand throats, every cub, every dwarf, every elf along the aisle, and under all of it a deeper roar rolling in from the streets, from the towns, from a whole continent watching the same sky.
Then a child's voice came up out of the cobbles.
"Rosie's turn!!"
It came out of the stone under the altar and out of every road on Iskaris at once, solemn and delighted in the same breath. Every soul standing on one of those roads heard it in the same moment.
"The Eternal Tree keeps her promise!"
High above the falling glass, the light changed.

A second pane laid itself across the sky where the first had stood, green-white and thin as breath, and it spread outward from the point above Miri Town in the same shape the crack had taken, until it covered the continent from horizon to horizon. For one heartbeat it caught the sun like a soap bubble.
Then it went clear, and there was nothing up there but blue.
"It's back?!"
"No, look, you can clearly see this one... it's-"
"Was that the princess? That was the little princess!"
Quinlan knew exactly what it was.
The Eternal Tree had promised him a barrier of her own in place of the old one, and the promise had come with its purpose written into it.
Whoever had laid the first wall over Iskaris, hundreds of thousands of years ago, would look at this continent from wherever they sat and see their claim standing exactly as they had left it.
Rosie's wall was a mirror facing outward. It held nobody in, it capped nobody's level, and it stood up there to lie to the outside world.
'And just like that, my daughter became the greatest fraudster in the world,' the Primordial Villain grinned inwardly, swelling with pride.
Then the window opened.
[Ding!]
[The prior claim over Iskaris has been dissolved.]
[The prior claim's domain has cleared. Suppression of sovereign faculties: lifted.]
Quinlan's eyes stopped on that line.
'There's more?'
Yesterday, at the beastkin fire, the universal system - the systemic interface all people were privy to - had notified him that the continent was his, and all he had felt was the land under his feet.
Roads like veins, cities like warmth, a coast he could point at with his eyes shut. He had taken that for the whole reward.
It had been the part of the gift that fit through the barrier of the hostile sovereign.
Now that it was gone...
The messages began bombarding his mind one after the other.
[Ding!]
[New title gained: Sovereign of Iskaris!]
[A Sovereign stands above a land's administrator. A Sovereign is the land's mightiest shield, and the land's sharpest spear.]
[No two Sovereigns rule the exact same way. This is reflected in their Sovereign Powers.]
[The Sovereign of Iskaris rules: One Land. Four Races.]
One land.
He read that line twice, and the grin that had been building since the sky cracked settled into the one his enemies knew.
'Only the beginning, huh?'
The way it was said told Quinlan there were other Sovereigns with more than one land to their names. 'What's the limit? Is there a limit? What are the rewards for holding more?'
The Primordial Villain's heart began pumping with pure excitement for the unknown.
[Ding!]
[Sovereign faculties initiating.]
[Sovereign Source: 100%.]
[The land tithes to its ruler. The Sovereign Source slowly refills on Sovereign Soil, and fills yet slower beyond it. Every active Sovereign ability cast draws upon it.]
[Ding!]
[New abilities gained!]
[Land's Strength: On Sovereign Soil, the Sovereign of Iskaris gains +25% on all attributes. The strength extends to those who carry the Sovereign's Bloodfather mark at +20%.]
[Domain Gate: Within Sovereign Soil, the Sovereign of Iskaris may open a gate to any point, at any size, in any number, whether or not the Sovereign has ever stood there.]

[Reign of the Undying: While the Sovereign of Iskaris reigns and the Soul Reaper endures, his Elite Souls return from destruction without [Awaken]. One return per soul per minute. When the Sovereign stands beyond his land, returned souls carry a 10% reduction with every resurrection until he sets foot on it again.]
[Boundless Dominion: On Sovereign Soil, the budget of [Subjugation] is limitless.]

[Elemental Host: The Sovereign of Iskaris may imbue one element over every soldier under the Sovereign's banner. There is no limit on their number. The Sovereign Source is drained 10% every minute Elemental Host is active.]

[Fire: every blade burns. Water: fatigue and thirst do not touch them. Earth: skin holds like stone. Wind: they move as the wind moves. Ice: whatever they strike slows. Lightning: they strike before the enemy finishes moving. Magma: their strikes gain unnatural weight.]

[Interdiction: Within Sovereign Soil, a rival Sovereign's faculties are throttled. The Sovereign of Iskaris may also raise a focused field of Interdiction at a cost, upon his own land or upon a Declaration.]

[Masked Seat: The Sovereign of Iskaris may mask himself. While masked, no domain reads the Sovereign of Iskaris as a Sovereign, and the concealment extends to those who carry his mark. A Declaration drops the mask.]
[Declaration of Conquest: The Sovereign of Iskaris may name a Sovereign's Land and declare his intention of conquest. The named sovereign is notified.]

[Upon a Declaration, the named Sovereign is granted 24 hours to prepare. Once those 24 hours have passed, the benefits of Declaration of Conquest manifest upon the targeted Sovereign Soil for 72 hours.]

[The named land's strength will be negated against the Sovereign and his marked; the Sovereign of Iskaris's Domain Gates open onto the named land; Interdiction may be raised upon it; the Sovereign Source fills rapidly upon it; Land's Strength is activated.]

[Should the term end before the named Sovereign falls: Land's Strength inverts across the Sovereign's own land; Domain Gate and Declaration are sealed; the Sovereign of Iskaris loses the Primordial Villain class. All of it holds until the named Sovereign falls.]
The barrage of windows finally stopped.
'Holy fuck.'
Quinlan stood under the white canopy, ten women holding onto him, ten thousand people screaming at a clear sky.
He was entirely speechless.
"Quin..." Ayame whispered, but her eyes weren't on him.
<You're seeing it too, huh?> Quinlan asked.
<Yeah... It says I'm recognized as your Empress.>
'Is it because of the Bloodfather class involving them?' Quinlan wondered. But he didn't care enough to mull on this. The more involved his girls were in this sovereign system, the better.
He would involve them either way. But having the system do it organically made everything that much better.
'Okay,' the Primordial Villain finally thought, having read his abilities a third time. 'Things just got real.'
The land answered in his shape.
Every power on that list was a power he already owned, grown to the size of a continent.
'All Sovereigns will wield unique powers...' Quinlan realized.

The barrage of windows finally stopped.
'Holy fuck.'
Quinlan stood under the white canopy, ten women holding onto him, ten thousand people screaming at a clear sky.
He was entirely speechless.
"Quin..." Ayame whispered, but her eyes weren't on him.
<You're seeing it too, huh?> Quinlan asked.
<Yeah...
It says I'm recognized as your Empress.>
'Is it because of the Bloodfather class involving them?' Quinlan wondered.
But he didn't care enough to mull on this.
The more involved his girls were in this sovereign system, the better.
He would involve them either way.
But having the system do it organically made everything that much better.
'Okay,' the Primordial Villain finally thought, having read his abilities a third time. 'Things just got real.'
The land answered in his shape.
Every power on that list was a power he already owned, grown to the size of a continent.
'All Sovereigns will wield unique powers...' Quinlan realized.

chapters.title: Chapter 1941 Personalized Abilities
paragraphs: [Domain Gate] was his [Warp Gate], the Primordial Villain's own spell, with its limits filed off. No more one gate at a time, small size, or borrowing a scout's eyes to reach anywhere new. Well, so long as it was inside Iskaris or a land was Declared.
[Masked Seat] was older than any class he held. He had masked himself for a very long time upon his arrival in Thalorind, enjoying the benefits of anonymity.

The system had taken that concealment and stretched it over the crown. Wherever he went, whoever's land he crossed, he would not be picked up by the enemy's sovereign senses, despite being a Sovereign himself.
If other Sovereigns had senses like these in their own lands, Quinlan knew that he'd be massacred as soon as he stepped on foreign soil. This circumvented that.
[Declaration of Conquest] was the Primordial Villain himself. A Villain announced what he was going to take, and then he took it.
'This is probably my ultimate card,' Quinlan mused.

[Reign of the Undying] was his necromancy, the Harbinger of Ruin's whole line: [Eternal Damnation], [Awaken], the Soul Reaper that ate what he killed, and the pale flame every soul soldier of his burned with.
Until today, a destroyed Elite Soul had cost him a recast and the mana behind it. Now the land itself would burn with that flame, and any soldier of his that fell on it would stand back up.

[Boundless Dominion] was the Primordial Subjugator. [Subjugation] had always come with a budget, a hundred points that the strong emptied faster than the weak. On Iskaris, he could bind as many as he wanted now.
[Elemental Host] was the Harbinger of Aeons, his seven elements manifested over his armies.
Now he could lay one over every soldier under his banner, from the soul army to the dwarven axes to the beastkin packs, all at once, with no ceiling on the number, and pay for it out of the Source.
And the rest of it was the Bloodfather.
'I bet [Land's Strength] would have been mine alone normally, if I was a maidenless loser. Perhaps with a slightly bigger personal boost to cope with the fact that my life is meaningless.'

The system had looked at the mark on ten wombs, and at the violet one Black Fang carried against a pillar at the edge of the square, and those he still accepted into the family despite not being his lovers, and decided that whatever the land gave him, it gave to them.
His family was the one part of the crown that was not about him.
[Land's Strength] itself, the Sovereign Source, and [Interdiction] were the crown's bones.
Every Sovereign in the world presumably held some version of those three. Everything else on the list was Quinlan Elysiar, spelled out in system text.
'The Suppression put over Iskaris sounds like a much stronger version of [Interdiction]... Perhaps suppressing others is that Sovereign's persona. What a sore loser,' Quinlan thought.
The last entry was the one with his name on it.
A Declaration was a bet. Name a Sovereign's land, hand its ruler a full day to ready themselves, and for the three days after that the land itself would hold the door for him.
Their strength dead against him and his marked, his gates opening onto their soil, his own Land's Strength alive under his boots on ground that was not his.

Lose the race against that clock, and Iskaris paid for it. His land's strength turned against him. His gates sealed shut. And the Primordial Villain class, the root every other power on that list grew from, was gone.
All of it, until the ruler he had named was dead or kneeling.
'An all-or-nothing battle to the death,' he chuckled. 'The system really does know me.'
[Ding!]
[Necromantic Tier Ascension: Tier III -> IV.]
'Finally.'

The Tier IV notification had frozen mid-sentence the day Aelindra Ael'vyrn died and rose again in blue, hung there flickering for one long second, and rewritten itself into a single instruction: break the suppression first.
Quinlan tried feeding his stored Lesser Souls into Scar through [Soul Fusion], to enhance her to Rank 6 status.
[Ding!]
[Lesser Souls of level 75 or above must be used as material.]
'...' Quinlan wasn't amused.
'No time to dwell,' the Primordial Villain quickly told himself before he got pissed off and started cursing the Soul Records on his wedding day.
The saber at his hip went hot.

It came through Synchra's living plate like a hand laid flat on his hipbone, and then the Soul Reaper was not asking anymore. The pitch-black blade pulled at him downward, toward the ground under the altar, with jealous insistence.
Quinlan drew it.
Ten thousand people went quiet in a wave that started at the altar and ran to the back streets, because the Emperor of Iskaris had just drawn his sword at his own wedding.
"Quin?" Ayame's hand had found his sleeve. "Is everything okay?"
"More than okay," he grinned, and reversed his grip.
He drove the Soul Reaper into the dais to the hilt.
Pale flame came up around the blade.

It was the same ghost-light his soul soldiers burned with, cold and blue-white, and it poured out of the buried saber in every direction at once. It ran across the dais, off its edge, into the cobbles of the square, and then it stopped being a fire and became a road.
"Let Rosie help!" Rosie shouted, and every root under Iskaris took the fire. Quinlan could feel his Necromantic flames traverse the lands along them, reaching the farthest parts within mere moments.
Every soul standing on a road felt it pass under their feet like a breath.
[Reign of the Undying: kindled.]
[Due to the Eternal Tree's assistance, its activation will cost no Sovereign Source.]
"Best daughter ever," Quinlan decreed while giving his leafy daughter the headpats she deserved.
"Hehehehe!!" Rosie beamed, leaning into her father's touch. She, too, was having a phenomenal day today.
The crowd of onlookers wasn't as amused.
"What did he do now?!"
"The roads are burning! Miri Town's on fire!"
"It's not hot, you fool, put your hand in it, it's not even-"
"Don't put your hand in it!! Are you retarded??"
At the far end of the square, where the Consortium row sat with their papers, the old Mediator had risen to his feet and was staring down at the pale flame lapping around his boots.
Beside him, Maelstrom had lifted both feet off the ground and was holding them there.
Quinlan pulled the Soul Reaper out of the dais.
The flame stayed where it was, burning in the roads with nothing to feed it, and the saber came up clean, dark, and pleased with itself.
Wherever that light ran, any Elite Soul of his could take a blade through the heart and stand up again a minute later without him lifting a finger.
'My home is now protected by a host of undying soldiers while I explore Thalorind,' the Primordial Villain thought, and sheathed the blade.
Then the girls felt an overwhelming sensation in their abdomens.
"Quin!!" Seraphiel yelped.
The Primordial Villain's wives would each be presented with a choice that could not be taken back.

chapters.title: Chapter 1942 Accept / Decline
paragraphs: Quinlan Elysiar had barely sheathed the Soul Reaper at the altar when the marks woke.
He felt it through the bond before he saw it: the Bloodfather marks warming on the skin of his family.
Around him, all of his women's eyes went unfocused at once, on windows only they could see.
[Ding!]
[You carry the Sovereign of Iskaris's mark!]
[Land's Strength: on Sovereign Soil, all attributes +20%.]
[Ding!]
The women who carried his mark on their wombs received a second notification.
[The Sovereign has named you Empress of Iskaris. Title granted: Empress of Iskaris.]
[The Sovereign's house is Elysiar.]
[Ayame Elysiar. Take the name? Accept / Decline.]
Ayame read it at his side with her hand still on his sleeve, and he watched her face do the thing it did before she cut something in half: absolute focus, then the decision.
"Accept," the Skysplitter said out loud, to the window and to him.
Down the line, nine more women were reading the same page.
"ACCEPT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!" Vex did not get past the first line, screaming from the bottom of her throat.
"Blossom accepts!! Blossom is Blossom Elysiar!!" The dogkin had no second name to give up, and neither did Vex. Lucille took hers to the end with both hands over her heart before she whispered yes.
"Kitsara Elysiar," Kitsara tried out loud, tails up. "Hmm. It makes me sound even more slutty. I love it."
"Yes," said Kaelira to the window, smiling fondly.
"Serika Elysiar..." Serika stopped and looked toward Rykar Vael below the dais on his four mechanical limbs. He sat straight and gave his daughter one slow, proud nod.
Serika winked back at him. "I'll always be your daughter." Then she grinned. "But I shall become a wonderful wife! Accept! Elysiar sounds richer anyway! Like I'm a proper lady."
"Aurora Lorien..." The alchemist glanced at the front row, where her father had started crying again, and accepted before he could get a word out.
"Yes," said Jasmine for the second time that day, and for the second time the gold came up in her eyes.
Only Sera had not answered.
The Dawnbringer stood with her lips pressed together and her blue eyes on the window, and Quinlan knew the face. It was the one she made when the elven rite and her own opinion disagreed.
"Quin..." Seraphiel sighed.

"There's nothing to feel bad about," Quinlan said, understanding. She was proud of her heritage and did not wish to lose the name her mother had given her. The Dawnbringer had already told him this a long time ago.
"..." She examined his face for a long moment, smiled brilliantly, then lifted her chin at the window. "Give me both."
The window considered that.
[Seraphiel Vaelorith Elysiar. Accept / Decline.]
"Accept," said the Dawnbringer.
Through the seam beside the altar, from her side of the stars, a squeal cut through that had nothing to do with rites.
"Nyxara Elysiar!!" Nyxara was shouting at Mimi. "Say it! Say it back to me! Nyxara Elysiar!"
"Nyxara Elysiar!!!" Mimi cheered, laughing. Especially when Nyxara lifted her with both arms, eyes streaking with tears, and begged, "Again!"
Mimi obliged.
But among those who wore the Bloodfather mark on their wombs, there was a sole exception.
Standing against her pillar at the edge of the square, Black Fang read a window with three lines fewer than everyone else's.
[The land you stand on has a Sovereign, and you carry his mark.]
[Land's Strength: on Sovereign Soil, all attributes +20%.]
The system offered the Venomborne Terror exactly what she had agreed to and not one line more. She read the two lines, closed the window, and looked at Quinlan with eyes of appreciation.
"Good," said Black Fang.
The boost landed.
It came up through the soles of their feet, and he felt all of them take it through the bond at once, every channel going hot together.
Serika's hair lifted off her shoulders and caught, red going white-gold at the tips.
Kitsara's tails fanned out behind her on their own and stayed there, every hair standing.
On the far side of the dais, Jasmine's seal blazed gold through white silk, and down the line every woman lit up in her own color.
The square saw it too. Ten thousand people watched ten women grow stronger in front of them in the space of a breath, and the sound out of the crowd this time had fear under it.
"The empresses..."
"Look at them! Look at the Solar Fist's hair!"
"Empresses!! Empresses!!"
The chant went out of the square into the streets and came back louder.
Against her pillar, Black Fang had not moved.

But the air around her had begun to rot, and the light dimmed at that edge of the square until the elves nearest her hugged themselves without knowing why. Her violet eyes had gone back up to the blue where the wall had been, swirling.
"..." Ayame had seen her sister's face from across the dais, and grinned. "Quin, look at big sis. She's going to kill something before the day is out."
"I know," the Primordial Villain grinned back. "She can finally level up again. I'm amazed she held back this long."
"Let's not waste more time," Ayame mused. "She won't hold for long. I think Maelstrom might get his head chopped off first."
The chant was still going when Quinlan opened the link.
[Master's Link] ran on the slave bond, and he narrowed it to the dais. The ten brides standing on it heard him.
<Girls,> he said, into ten heads at once. <Before anyone gets to ask us anything. Let's keep the details within the family.>
While Quinlan had been open recently toward the general populace of Iskaris, such as speaking up about his mothers, his goals, and more, he had no intentions of becoming an open book.
Now that the stakes had risen to levels he still didn't quite comprehend, it was even more so the case.
<Thalorind has opened up to us, and it's now time to act like we did in the beginning,> Ayame whispered into all their heads. Her voice was buzzing with excitement.
<This is so exciting~> Lucille purred. <Time to wear masks once again?>
<I don't know about literal masks again, but yeah. We have to take things very seriously,> Quinlan nodded.

Serika was in agreement as well. <For all we know, there are people out there much higher statted than we are, with classes and powers we aren't prepared for. Best not to let them get info on us from our allies.>

<...> Silence reigned supreme on the link for a good few seconds, as every participant buzzed with sheer excitement for the grand unknown that awaited them outside the only land they knew all their lives.
<Feed us the juice, Quinnie!> Kitsara purred. <You can't hog all your notifications to yourself! Tell me your stats!>
<Sure.>
He opened it.
[Name: Quinlan Elysiar]
[Race: Primordial]
[Land's Strength: active. All attributes +25%.]
[Health Points: 4688]
[Mana Points: 5625]
[Vitality: 313]
[Strength: 253]
[Agility: 266]
[Magic: 375]
Sixty-five. Seven levels for the many weeks he spent grinding the labyrinth religiously.
Take the land buff away and the Vitality line read two hundred and fifty, the Magic line three hundred. The other quarter was the crown, and it came free with every step he took on his own soil.
<Three hundred and seventy-five Magic,> he said, widening the link one head, into eleven at once, Iris included.
<...Okay,> Serika said. <That's more than Morgana's.>
<Hmm. I gotta say I married well,> Kitsara decided. <Maybe I should write a 'how to throw yourself at the exact right man for a prosperous future'? It might become a bestseller.>
<Hubby,> Vex cut in, everyone ignoring the foxy's thought process. <What should I do if I'm falling in love all over again? But I haven't stopped loving you for a single moment?!>
<...Perhaps this will help,> Quinlan smirked and faced the front rows.
"You'll all want to see this one. Come with us."
"See what?" Skarn's hackles had never fully come down since the sky cracked.
"The edge of the world."
Quinlan reached into the land with the thing that had woken under his boots at the beastkin fire, the sense that ran through every road and field of Iskaris now.
He found the nearest stretch of coast his land could feel, a shore he had never once stood on, and opened a gate to it.

[Magic: 375]
Sixty-five.
Seven levels for the many weeks he spent grinding the labyrinth religiously.
Take the land buff away and the Vitality line read two hundred and fifty, the Magic line three hundred.
The other quarter was the crown, and it came free with every step he took on his own soil.
<Three hundred and seventy-five Magic,> he said, widening the link one head, into eleven at once, Iris included.
<...Okay,> Serika said.
<That's more than Morgana's.>
<Hmm.
I gotta say I married well,> Kitsara decided.
<Maybe I should write a 'how to throw yourself at the exact right man for a prosperous future'?
It might become a bestseller.>
<Hubby,> Vex cut in, everyone ignoring the foxy's thought process.
<What should I do if I'm falling in love all over again?
But I haven't stopped loving you for a single moment?!>
<...Perhaps this will help,> Quinlan smirked and faced the front rows.
"You'll all want to see this one.
Come with us."
"See what?" Skarn's hackles had never fully come down since the sky cracked.
"The edge of the world."
Quinlan reached into the land with the thing that had woken under his boots at the beastkin fire, the sense that ran through every road and field of Iskaris now.
He found the nearest stretch of coast his land could feel, a shore he had never once stood on, and opened a gate to it.

chapters.title: Chapter 1943 Sandy Beach
paragraphs: Dark light stood up out of the square's own cobbles in a single sheet, taller than the great doors and wide enough that the front rows had to step back from it. Through it lay blue sky and moving water.
Ayame looked at it, then at him.
"Quin."
"What can I say? Being a ruler rules," Quinlan mused slyly, not elaborating.
Of course, he'd share his abilities with the girls without holding anything back. But messing with his cheeky samurai was one of the Villain's favorite activities.
"You're not funny one bit. Hmph."
Ayame Elysiar stepped through the gate first, arms crossed under her delicate chest.
The shore was white sand and slow waves rolling in, and past where they broke the water went blue all the way out to a sky with nothing in it but the sun.
The powers of the continent stepped out of a wall of light onto their beach.
First the empresses, then Rosie, who ran straight to the water's edge to look at her own wall from underneath and reported that she could not see it.

After them came the governor of Elysaria, a queen of fourteen with her father the retired king behind her, four beastkin lords with their hackles up, a dwarf in a formal coat, two Fujimori, the Obsidian Circle in a nervous row, the Scarlet Lilies, and Iris.
Black Fang stepped through last.
"Wait, wait, where even is this?!" Felicity demanded of the waves.
"The southern coast," Alexios replied before Quinlan could, knowing his land like the back of his hand.
Seraphiel had stopped listening at the first step.
The Dawnbringer stood with her eyes closed and her bare feet dug into the sand to the ankle, and the sound she made belonged in a bedroom.
"Quin," she whispered, without opening her eyes. "It's so warm..."
Iskaris had never lacked for beaches. On most of them a person could walk into the water and take a few steps before the Restriction sent them back.
But those beaches weren't as immaculate as this one. Here the wall had stood a few steps short of the water, and the sand past it had never carried a footprint.
Seraphiel's toes curled. "Girls, get your shoes off and come here. I can't have my sister-wives miss this."
Kitsara and Blossom had theirs off before the sentence ended. Lucille walked in beside the elf, sank to her ankles, and made the same shameless sound.
"Told you," Sera sighed, wriggling deeper. "This is the best beach ever! We need to organize a swimsuit party when we have the time."
"Swimsuit party?" Aurora hummed, sinking in with her friends. "Ah, yes, I remember. One of Quin's pervy fantasies. Have us dress in skimpy clothes and let him put suncream on us..."
"Exactly!" Sera beamed, having remembered her lover's fetishes with crystal clarity.
"No objections from me~" Serika was instantly game. Sandy, hot beaches sounded right up her alley. Having Quinlan get oily with her was just the cherry on top.
As the girls enjoyed the beach, Ayame was staring at the water ahead.
"You know the barrier's rule," she said. "You walk into the sea, you black out, and you wake up on the sand a few paces back with a headache and wet boots."
"I've been told that nearly every child in the coastal settlements tries it at least once," Alexios said. "It's a fun game for them."
"I tried it a dozen times," said Rajah.

"More than a hundred..." whispered Lilith. After reaching level 74, her life's mission became escaping the Heavenly Restriction so that she could resume her leveling journey. This was the reason why the Lilies agreed to help Kaede and the Fujimori clan in the first place.
"More than a hundred thousand," muttered Black Fang under a shaky breath.
"I spent centuries studying this phenomenon..." spoke the Mediator. Both of his legs were trembling so hard that two of the Obsidian Circle had to hold him up.
"I'm afraid your research material became unavailable, old man," Quinlan smirked as he began walking forward.
Synchra flared between the first and second step as Quinlan shrugged her off.

The black wedding suit went crimson at every seam and ran off him like water, off his shoulders, down his chest, down his legs, until it gathered at his left ankle into a thin black band with a single red seam, humming.
Synchra was sulking. He could feel it against the bone, a small jealous vibration from a suit of armor that had just been demoted from a wedding suit to an ankle bracelet.
The Primordial Villain stood on the sand of his continent wearing an anklet and nothing else.
"Uhh..." Jallen seemed to have found something difficult to grasp while observing Quinlan from behind. "What's that giant thing dangling between his legs?"
"Oh my," said Void, and opened one eye, which for Void was a standing ovation.
"No wonder the serpent likes him so much." Lilith jabbed at Black Fang. Luckily for her, the Venomborne Terror was not in a mental state to listen to her.
Even before she said it, the captain of the Scarlet Lilies had already clamped a hand over her niece's eyes. "Stop squirming, Felicity."
"Aunt Lilith! I'm the queen!" Felicity was prying at the fingers with both hands, up on her toes. "I've seen statues!"
"Statues don't swing like that. It's obscene."
"I command you!! Let me see!!"
"I'll leave on an adventure within hours, so Your Majesty may banish me freely."
"N-not fair!!"
"This guy..." Ayame sighed, shaking her head. Despite her best efforts, she was grinning from ear to ear.
"Hubby will remain Hubby, Sovereign or not~" Vex purred, eyes laser focused.
"Master's butt..." Blossom Elysiar was about to begin salivating.
Kitsara put two fingers in her mouth and whistled loud enough to carry across the whole beach. "Do a swirl, handsome!!"
Down the line, the governor of Elysaria was looking, kept looking, and then licked her lips. "That brings back memories..." Myrasyn muttered, mind back in a dark cell.
Quinlan walked down the sand.
The first wave broke over his bare feet, cold, and the Primordial Villain kept walking, water climbing his ankle, his shin, his knee.
Behind him a wave washed up the sand and slid back down it. The next one was already rolling in at him, and the beach had gone so quiet that the water was the only sound.
He walked past the line where every Iskarian who had ever tried had gone black and woken on the sand, no matter where on the continent.
Nothing took him.
The water took his thighs, then his waist, and the waves shoved at his chest. He leaned into it, kept going, and when it reached his collarbone he stopped and turned around.
The powers of Iskaris were strung along the sand in a ragged line, and every face on it had gone slack, mouths open.
Rosie found her voice first.
"Rosie's wall let Daddy through!" she screamed at the whole beach, jumping. "Whichever Mommy doesn't go swimming should consider pampering Rosie!!"
And the beach broke the way the square had.
Serika hit the water at a sprint, while Felicity shrieked and grabbed Feng by both arms.
Lilith Ravenshade sat down hard where she stood, both hands flat on the sand, and then howled at the sky, no words in it, until she ran out of breath.
The Mediator had slipped out of the Circle's hands and onto his knees in the sand, grey eyes on the water, tears running into his beard.
The four lords stayed where the water ended, staring past him at a horizon none of them had ever been allowed to reach.
"...I'll be damned," Gorruk the bearkin said, very quietly.
Rajah had not blinked since the first wave. "A dozen times," the tigerkin said to nobody, and then again, louder, with a laugh in it. "A dozen times!"
Black Fang walked into the water to her shins and stopped there.
The Venomborne Terror stood in the shallows with her black attire soaked to the knee, and then she bent down, slowly, and put her hand into the sea.
The water ran over her fingers and out again. She cupped what she could, lifted it to the sun, and watched it run out between her knuckles and fall, speechless.
Four hundred years.
It was over.
She was free.

chapters.title: Chapter 1944 Scouting the Ocean
paragraphs: Quinlan studied the water around him.

They had just agreed that Thalorind might contain monsters far beyond them. He was delighted to have an ocean at his disposal, but he wanted to know what was in it before taking his wives farther out.
Through his feet in the sand, he sent his earth magic through the seabed. The shore continued beneath the waves, sloping toward a broken shelf, and he followed its shape down into the rock.

Hollows opened in his awareness, then ridges, then the deep cut where the shelf ended. He had used this same sense to read footsteps through the dwarves' mountain. Here, he wanted to find the places a creature could hide.
"Quin?" Sera called from the beach.
"A moment. I'm scouting."

Quinlan pulled the sea away from the beach with his water magic. The retreating water exposed a widening stretch of seabed before piling up above the shelf, where he held it in an enormous curved wall.
Wet sand stretched out before him, broken by the ridges he had mapped through the earth. Farther out, fish darted inside the suspended water, high above what had been the surface of the sea.
"What the fuck?!" Maelstrom stumbled back from the tideline. "Is that coming this way?!"
"I'm holding it there," Quinlan assured the onlookers, examining the exposed rocks. "I'd like to see what's hiding ahead."
Then, under his breath, he muttered, "Seen enough freaky shark movies to know caution is my best friend here..."

His earth magic had found hollows beneath those rocks. Quinlan drew narrow streams from the wall and sent them into each opening, washing out the silt while he searched for anything resisting the flow.
He could inspect the water itself too. By drawing currents through the suspended mass, he sensed the fish pushing against his magic as they swam, each body displacing water he controlled.
"He's searching underneath the rocks..." Jallen murmured, watching a stream emerge from a hole in the seabed. She craned her neck toward the towering wall again. "While holding all of that?"
Quinlan smiled as he checked the last hollow. His family would have a stretch of sand and harmless fish beneath their feet. Anything that wanted to eat them would have to come from farther out.
Once he was satisfied, he began lowering the wall.
The onlookers braced for the crash.

Quinlan eased the water down, spreading it over the exposed seabed until the sea returned to the shore. Jallen watched a gentle wave lap at her toes, then turned to the man who had just put the ocean back without splashing her.

He maintained control of a thin curtain of water around the area he had cleared. It curved from one end of the beach to the other, enclosing the swimming area, and extended from the surface all the way down to the seabed.

Farther out, beyond the shelf, he formed a second, wider curtain of controlled water. An approaching creature would have to pass through that outer boundary, cross the water between them, then breach the inner one to reach his family.

The two curtains were submerged, made from the same seawater as everything around them. The onlookers could see ordinary waves rolling toward the beach, but Quinlan would feel anything pushing through the water he held.
A fish crossed the outer curtain, tugging at his magic. He read its size and direction from the water it displaced, then sensed it again when it moved through the inner curtain closer to shore.
Quinlan smiled. There it was.
Then a much heavier body pressed against the far side of his outer boundary. Quinlan followed its movement through his magic as it turned away, swimming back toward deeper water.
"What are you feeling?" Ayame asked, watching him now.
"Something big just brushed against the water I'm holding out there. Probably a sea monster." He glanced toward the distant disturbance. "It's heading away from us."

He left a curve of white foam above the inner curtain, just inside the shelf, to mark how far they could go. Beneath the cleared water, he prepared broad currents pointing back toward the beach, ready to carry his family ashore if the warning came.
"It's far from the shore, and I made preparations. I'll know if anything tries to come closer."
The net would give him time to react. He intended to use that time to get his women out of danger before finding out how strong their visitor was.
Even an invisible monster would still displace water, and a fast one would have to cross the distance between his two boundaries. Quinlan was confident he would feel either one coming.
With the net in place, he waded over to Black Fang, who had scooped up another handful of seawater and was watching it drain between her fingers.
She had tried to escape Iskaris more than a hundred thousand times. Now the ocean lay open before her, and she was standing in the shallows trying to comprehend that she could actually walk into it.
Quinlan wanted to take her much farther than that.
"Will you come with me, Black Fang?" he asked, smiling, offering her his extended arm. "Let's enjoy this together."

"..." Black Fang angled her neck back, looking up at him. The wonder in her eyes almost made Quinlan's heart skip a beat. 'Truly, what a woman...' he noted, once more. Then grinned inwardly. 'Man, I just can't stop simping when it comes to her.'
After a second that felt like a minute, staring into his deep eyes, Black Fang clasped his offered hand.
Her fingers tightened around his as they passed the depth that had defeated her for centuries.
Quinlan walked on until the water was at their waists. Behind them, Ayame was calling to her sister, but Black Fang seemed to have forgotten the beach existed.
She gazed past the waves toward a horizon she could finally reach. The black silk floated around her hips as she pressed forward, impatient with the water pushing against her.
"Farther."
Quinlan laughed and let her pull him along. He'd brought her out here to enjoy herself, and watching her try to drag him into the ocean was already making his day.
"Big sis! Wait for me!!"
Ayame came splashing after them with her wedding skirt gathered in both hands. She passed the old limit before she remembered to look down, then beamed at the others.
"Girls, come! You have to try this!"
His wives were happy to oblige.
"Blossom isn't good with water!!" Blossom yelped, tail going limp.
"Foxies are truly supreme then, for this graceful empress has no trouble getting wet at all!" Kitsara crowed, running to her husband.
"Ngg!!" Blossom, too, braced herself after exchanging a glance with her Master. "Master!" His mere smile and confident gaze ensured she leaped right into his arms.
Soon they were all crowding around him in the water, laughing as their skirts floated up around their legs and catching each other whenever a wave tried to knock them over.
Quinlan had married some of the most dangerous women on the continent, and right now they were arguing about whether to take their dresses off. Several seemed ready to start swimming in them.
He loved these women so fucking much.
"I have a better idea," he announced, then shouted towards the beach. "Rosie! Can you grow us some boards? Long, flat ones, with the front curved up?"
"Easy!!"
