chapters.title: Chapter 1945 Surfing with the Wives
paragraphs: His daughter planted her hands in the wet sand, and pale roots came bursting out around her. They broadened into smooth wooden boards, each one parting from its stem with a crack before another grew in its place.
Quinlan drew them out to his wives on the water. Ayame grabbed the first and laid herself across it, her bare feet kicking behind her as it carried her over a swell.
"What are we doing with these?"
"Surfing. I'll make you a wave, and you see how long you can stay on top of it."
"Oh, that sounds fun!" Serika snatched up a board and hugged it against her chest. "Make mine a big one, Quin!"
"On our feet?" Vex asked, pushing herself up on her board. She studied the wood beneath her, then the waves farther out. "I have to try this~"
"Let me guess." Ayame's eyes narrowed, though the edge of her lips refused to fall into line. The delicate samurai was grinning hopelessly as she said, "You'll come with us and show off."
"Show off?" Quinlan chuckled. "I wouldn't dare. I just want to enjoy the waves with my beloved wives."
"Hmph." She reached for his arm to pull him closer. "Then you'd better teach me."
"With a joyous heart," Quinlan replied. "Synchra. Let's go."
Synchra tightened around his ankle in answer. Quinlan looked down at the black band, amused. His armor had taken the demotion from wedding suit to anklet very personally.
"Will you help me, partner?"
A second passed, then another.

Then the anklet came apart in a rush of living metal that spread across the surface. Synchra formed a sleek black board beneath him, crimson seams glowing along its curved nose, and Quinlan climbed aboard.
"I'm forever grateful."
Synchra hummed beneath his soles.
Quinlan retrieved the Soul Reaper from his ring too, holding the saber out over the waves.

The blade tugged at his fingers, eager to be released, and he let it go with a chuckle. It flew alongside him for a moment before dipping into the sea, cutting through a crest that promptly collapsed over his head.
"Papa!! Rosie wants to come too!"
His daughter was waving at him from the sand. Quinlan used wind magic to grab onto the green lady and bring her to him.
"Rosie wants her throne!!"
"After today, you certainly deserve this much," Quinlan chuckled, making Rosie beam with overwhelming joy.
He lifted her under the arms and settled her on his shoulders, her legs hanging down his chest. Rosie gripped two fistfuls of his hair and took in the sea, thrilled with the improvement.
"Rosie can see all the mommies!"
"Then you can help me ensure none of them are left behind."
"Rosie will report everything!" she announced, her hands making a miniature telescope as she diligently scouted her mothers.
Quinlan kissed her knee before taking her ankles in his hands. His daughter was sitting on his shoulders, his brides were gathering around him, and he had the sea to play with.
He was going to enjoy this afternoon to the fullest.
With a pull of his water magic, Quinlan brought all their boards into a loose curve facing Synchra.
"Ah! I'm not made for this!" Jasmine caught Aurora's hand as their boards bumped together.
"H-hey, don't cling to me!" Aurora yelped in return, then the two women somehow managed to hug each other as they helplessly began falling toward the water like a domino.
But before the water could soak their dresses, Quinlan steadied them both with his wind.
"..." Aurora's eyes were pointedly narrowed toward Jasmine once the pair was once again standing upright on their boards.
"S-sorry..." Jasmine giggled, cheeks slightly pink.
Aurora soon dropped the act, joining her cherished friend in laughter.
"Watch my feet," Quinlan spoke up, beginning the instructions. "One ahead of the other, near the middle. Keep your knees bent so you can adjust when the board moves."
He raised a gentle swell beneath them and leaned across its slope, letting Synchra turn under his weight.
"That's how you steer. I'll give you a little wave to start with."
"Little sounds wonderful," Aurora decided.
Jasmine stood beside her, eyed the wobbling board, and immediately reached for Quinlan.
"My love, perhaps a hand would- ah!"
Her board tipped as she stretched across the gap. Quinlan caught her with wind once again, then used water to perfectly set the board beneath her before lowering the woman down onto it once again.
This time, the governor of the grand Iskaris Empire bit her lip in full focus, refusing to embarrass herself a third time.
Rosie bent over his head to inspect Jasmine's feet, her hair falling into his eyes.
"Jasmine Mommy is standing!"
"Jasmine Mommy would like to stay standing, sweetheart," the governor replied, then giggled again when her board rocked. "Kya!!"
She held Quinlan's hand until the wobbling stopped, then released him to try a turn of her own.
Beside her, Aurora knew which way she needed to lean, but kept correcting too late, her arms swinging wider with every wobble.
"Quin! How are you meant to turn when it keeps-"
*Splash!*
"Oh, for fuck's sake!"
Quinlan used his water magic to set a screen of foam between his wet wife and the onlookers, hiding her gorgeous body until he dried her dress within moments.
"As possessive as ever..." Aurora giggled, holding onto him.
Lucille grabbed Aurora's board and brought it back to her, smiling sympathetically.
"Would you like to try beside me? I think I got the hang of it."
"Already?!" Aurora's eyes widened. Then she, too, steeled her resolve. "Yes, please."
On Quinlan's other side, Ayame had already found her balance.
The samurai gathered her skirt clear of her feet and leaned into her first turn, cutting across the face of the swell with an eager grin.
She glanced back at him as she passed, plainly waiting to see whether he had noticed.
"As expected of my acrobat of a samurai~" Quinlan mused, making Ayame pause, for his face held a lot more emotion for her person than she had expected.
"Shall I make it steeper?" he offered.
"...Sure! I want to see how far I can lean!"
Quinlan raised the water ahead of her, and Ayame drove her board up its slope. White silk fluttered around her legs as she turned at the top, coming back down with a triumphant laugh.
"Did you see that?!"
"Rosie saw!!!"
"I certainly did," Quinlan agreed, admiring his beautiful bride. "Again?"
"Of course again~"
Serika was already coming up behind her. His former teacher had stood on her first attempt, adjusted her feet, and begun asking what else the board could do.
Now she planted one hand on its nose and swung her legs over herself, her red ponytail flying through the spray.
"Why is the fire chick so good in water? This should be my domain," Ayame observed as Serika landed facing backward.
"She's always been the coolest one..." Aurora offered.
"It's fun!!" Serika whooped. "Quin, can you give us a bigger wave?!"
He happily obliged. The wave rose beneath both women, and Serika dropped into a low, loose stance while Ayame took the higher line.
Quinlan watched their strong legs carry them through the turns, wedding silk billowing behind them. His wives were fucking magnificent, and they knew exactly how much he was enjoying the sight.
Ayame caught his gaze as spray struck her skirt. He drew the water away, and her chin rose with a pleased smile.
"You're very happy with yourself, hmm?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1946 Joyous Day
paragraphs: "After all the warfare and politics, this is pure heaven," Quinlan grinned, hiding none of his thoughts. "I missed being with my girls like this."
"Hehe!" Sera was doing her best to keep up. "Kaeli, let's do this."
"T-trying!"

"Hmm, I'm getting the hang of this," Vex spoke with slightly more volume than required. This had the planned result of Quinlan glancing her way, which the Hexwitch rewarded with a gorgeous smile toward her lover.
"This is so fun, Hubby... Wait, is this our honeymoon?"

"This is the warm-up." Quinlan's eyes shone with a glint his women knew far too well. A greedy primordial's mounting desire to explore. "Our real honeymoon will be venturing into Thalorind proper and wreaking havoc."
"Can't wait~" Vex purred.
"Faster, Daddy! Rosie wants to go with the Mommies! If she knew her Papa would just stand still while yapping, Rosie would've sat on her Mommies instead!"

"You want speed, huh?" Quinlan tightened his hands around his daughter's ankles and sent Synchra after them. Rosie shrieked with laughter as they climbed the wave, leaning forward until her chin rested on top of his head.
"Higher!!!"
"Like this?"
He brought their wave up beside Ayame's, and Rosie squealed her approval straight into his ear.
Quinlan laughed with her. His daughter's delight was making it very difficult to resist giving her every wave she asked for.
Around them, he still felt the two curtains of water he controlled. Fish brushed through the outer boundary, and he tracked each disturbance while his little girl demanded another turn.
Sera was riding farther down the beach, golden hair streaming behind her as she spread her arms into the wind.
"Quin, can I go all the way to that end?!"
"Along the shore, yes. I'll bring your wave around."
He extended the swell beneath her board, curving it inside the marked boundary. The Dawnbringer let out a joyous scream, then laughed so hard she had to bend over to keep her balance.
"Kaelira! Come with me!"
The smith was standing now, carefully testing how far she could tilt the wood. She glanced up at her best friend, smiling uncertainly.
"I haven't tried going that fast..."
"Want a hand? We'll do it together~"
Quinlan guided their boards alongside each other, and Kaelira reached for Sera. With her friend beside her, the elf leaned into the next swell, her smile growing as they picked up speed.
"Ah... wait, this is fun!" Kaelira realized as she started getting the hang of it.
"I know!"
Seeing how far they'd come, they began laughing together. Kaelira's navy hair blew across her face, and for once the shy elf was loud enough for everyone to hear her.
Quinlan wanted to hear that much more often.
"Papa! Look!"
Rosie tugged his hair to turn his head. Jasmine was coming toward them, knees bent, both arms out for balance, while Aurora rode beside Lucille on the next swell.
"My love! I'm doing it!"
"My governor is far too amazing, too. No one is a mere pencil pusher in this family," Quinlan laughed.
The governor beamed. "That's right! Watch this!" She let her board turn across the wave, wobbling once before correcting herself, and came past him laughing with relief.
Aurora followed a moment later, her concentration breaking into a grin as she rode into calmer water.
"Alright. I understand why you girls keep screaming now."
"Another one?" Lucille asked, already turning her board.
"Yes."

Vex swept past them with Blossom following close behind. The Hexwitch was leaning forward for speed, white hair flying through the spray, while the dogkin kept looking down at the water beside her feet.
"Hubby! Rosie! Look over here!"
"Rosie sees both mommies!!"
Blossom looked up at Quinlan with her ears drooping.
"Is Blossom doing it right, Master?"
"You're doing wonderfully. How does it feel?"
"Wobbly!!"
She tried to follow Vex down the wave, leaning too sharply into the turn. The edge of her board caught the water, swinging the wood sideways beneath her feet.
"Ah! M-Master!!"

Blossom kicked off the tilting board, launching herself high above the wave. Her dress billowed around her as she tucked into a backward somersault, then a second, then a third, blonde hair and tail whirling through the air.
Below her, the board slid free of the turn and skimmed down the swell. Blossom opened out above it, planted both feet on the wood, and bent her knees to absorb the landing.
Her board glided past Quinlan with its nose pointing neatly down the wave.
"Hah... Hah...! That was close!!!"
Blossom stayed crouched, panting with her hands on her knees. The fright had left her heart pounding, and she looked up at her husband with genuine relief.
"Master!! Blossom almost fell!!"
Aurora stared at her. Beside the alchemist, Jasmine had stopped trying to turn her board.
"...Almost," Aurora repeated. "How terrible for you."
Jasmine looked from the perfectly balanced dogkin to Aurora, her mouth twisting wryly.
"I think I pulled something trying to stand up."
"I swallowed seawater."
The two women watched Blossom straighten, still fussing over her footing as her board rode effortlessly over another swell.
Life was unfair.
"Blossom Mommy flew!!" Rosie shrieked, bouncing on Quinlan's shoulders. "Three times!!"
Quinlan was grinning hopelessly at his dogkin lover. His adorable assassin had just turned a stumble into a triple backflip, and she was worried she'd done a poor job.
"That was incredible, Blossom."
"...It was?"
Her ears perked up, though she kept shifting her gaze between him and the board beneath her.
"I could watch you do that all day."
"Master liked it?"
"It was pure badassery. Very sexy," Quinlan nodded solemnly. He then moved Synchra alongside her, keeping one hand around Rosie's ankle while he reached out to stroke Blossom's head with the other.
"My super talented Pupcake cannot stop impressing me~"
Blossom nuzzled eagerly into his palm. Knowing she had impressed him made her so happy that she forgot to worry about the water, her fluffy tail wagging behind her as she beamed up at her Master.
"Blossom will keep practicing!!"
Vex circled back toward them, and Blossom followed her onto the next wave, smiling this time.
"Vex, teach Blossom!!"
"...Shouldn't it be the other way around?" Vex asked wryly.
"No, Vex is much better!! Blossom can barely stand straight!"
"Haaah... You hopeless girl. Alright, follow my lead!" Vex smiled, and the two took off.
His girls were getting used to the sea. They were choosing their turns, reaching for each other, calling back to the people on the beach to watch them.
Then a board would carry one of them farther out, and she would look down in fresh amazement at the open water beneath her.
They were free to be here. Quinlan felt Jasmine's happiness through the bond as she took another turn, and gave Rosie a gentle squeeze when his daughter cheered her on.
'What a blissful existence,' Quinlan sighed inwardly, taking the entire sight in. 'This is why I must fight. This is why I cannot stop growing.'
In this moment, the Primordial Villain steeled his heart.
'No matter what, I must reach a state of supremacy. I must protect them all.'
With that, it was time to enjoy the waves a little more, then take the first step into distant lands!

chapters.title: Chapter 1947 Could've Been Worse
paragraphs: Quinlan rode Synchra along the southern shore, smiling as his wives called to one another across the waves.
"Daddy's gone quiet!" Rosie noticed from her perch on his shoulders.
"Just enjoying the moment."
"Quinnie~ Your empress requests a kiss!"
Kitsara brought her board alongside Synchra, her five white tails fanned out behind her.
The foxy leaned toward him, tilted her board too far, and promptly tumbled off it.
"Kyaa!"
Quinlan raised a screen of foaming water before she surfaced. Kitsara emerged with her ears flat and her hair covering her eyes, reaching for him through the spray.
"You didn't catch me on purpose! How could you???"
"A baseless accusation."
Quinlan crouched carefully on Synchra, keeping one hand around Rosie's ankle as he offered the other to Kitsara.
"Hmph! The jury finds the defendant guilty!" The foxy clasped his hand and rested against his knee while his magic drained the water from her clothes.

"The sentence is giving me a big smooch..." She pulled herself up far enough to kiss him, and Quinlan bent to meet her, smiling at his shameless bride. He lifted her back onto her board with a curl of water, then straightened with Rosie perched on his shoulders.
Once she was dry, he lowered the screen. Kitsara immediately spotted her father watching from the shore and waved at him with both arms.
"Father! Did you see me riding the wave?"
"Yes," Vargis called back. "Very good! Perhaps pay attention to where you're going!"
"Ah!"
Kitsara saved herself from a second fall. Quinlan laughed, sending her board along on a gentler swell while she rediscovered the benefits of paying attention.

The Soul Reaper shot past Quinlan's shoulder, cutting a crest apart before darting underneath the falling water. The blade was celebrating their newfound freedom just as his girls were. Though it might've been mostly excited about the bloodshed it knew would certainly follow.
Rosie shrieked with laughter when the spray reached them.
"Again!!"
The saber circled back through the foam, and Black Fang rode out behind it.
After studying the others, she understood the board. Now she was crouched low over it, black silk streaming behind her as she banked sharply.
Quinlan rolled a fresh swell toward her. She rode up its slope, trailed her fingers through the curling water, then glanced back at him with an expression that made him stare.
Black Fang was enjoying herself so much that her mask of cold indifference was slipping.
Her violet eyes were bright, her lips pursed together as she studied the waves Ayame and Serika were getting. She was eager for one like that too.
Quinlan built it for her, feeling far too happy to be the man she kept turning to for more.
"Big sis!" Ayame cried, delighted. "You're smiling!!"
The Venomborne Terror regarded her sister.
"You are seeing things."
"Quin sees it too! Look at him!"
She looked. Her eyes were murderous.
"...I see nothing," Quinlan announced.
Ayame burst out laughing. "Come on!"
Black Fang turned away from both of them. She was facing the sea once more.
On the beach, Lilith Ravenshade was watching the women when Void climbed onto her back.
The mage hooked her arms around the captain's shoulders and clasped her legs around Lilith's waist, resting her chin beside her neck with her eyelids half closed.
She pointed at the sea.
"What?" Lilith twisted her head toward the mage. "Get down. I'm not your horse."
"My shark...?"
Bronnya was chuckling behind them. Jallen saw her captain look back toward the waves, then picked up one of the spare boards from the sand.
"We could try it together."
"In these clothes?"
"The brides are literally in their wedding dresses."
Lilith glanced toward the surfers. Serika was riding down a steep wave with her arms spread, laughing at something Ayame had shouted to her.
The captain wanted to be out there so badly that her hands were shaking.
She had tried to escape the Restriction more than a hundred times. She had yearned for her next level, a new place to hunt, a direction she could walk without being thrown back.
Now a child was offering planks of wood, and people were riding over the place that had defeated her for centuries.
Void knew what that meant to her. She settled more comfortably against her captain and kept pointing toward the waves.
"...A board," Lilith said at last, looking toward Rosie on Quinlan's shoulders. "Could we have a board?"
"There!"
Rosie pointed back at the shore. Roots burst from the wet sand beside the captain, spreading into a board wide enough for her and her passenger. More grew beside it for Bronnya and Jallen.
"Hold on," Lilith muttered to Void as she grabbed the first one.
"...Already am."
The captain waded into the shallows with her board, put it down, and stepped aboard. Quinlan brought a wave under it, waiting while she found her balance with Void hanging off her back.
Lilith looked down as her board carried her farther from shore.
The sand was still receding beneath her. Her knees bent as the swell lifted, and she gazed up at the open sea with a disbelieving smile.
"Fuck..."
Then she tipped her weight forward.

Quinlan built the wave, and Lilith went with it, silver strands tearing free of her collar as her board accelerated. Bronnya drew level on her left, Jallen on her right, all three adjusting to each other's turns.
"Bahahaha!! Boss! This is fucking great!!"
Lilith was grinning wildly.
Quinlan floated one of Rosie's spare boards out to the Lilies and cast [Awaken] above it. Pale flame gathered into Scar, her blue skin and familiar mask drawing an immediate shout from Bronnya.
"Scar! Over here!"
The soul general faced Quinlan, finding her balance on the moving wood instantly.
"Master?"
"A short break," he offered.
"...Okay," Scar muttered under her breath, visibly confused. Things were moving too fast even for the legendary leader of the Villain's necromantic forces.
"Want a wave?" Quinlan smiled.
He guided her after her old teammates, and Void lifted her chin from Lilith's shoulder to watch Scar approach.
"Mount swap time..." she announced.
"Give her a chance to enjoy the waves," Jallen laughed.
"Hmph..." The Void Mage perfectly replicated Rosie's pout.
Lilith cut across the wave to make room for Bronnya, and Jallen slipped through the spray behind them. Scar claimed the open stretch beside the captain as Quinlan made the swell steeper.
Lilith drove her board up the slope until its nose broke clear of the crest. For a moment she and Void hung above the spray, the mage's feet dangling at the captain's sides.
Then Lilith turned her hips, brought the board around beneath them, and dropped back down the wave.
Void's arms tightened around her shoulders. "Orc boss is getting too heated... Help..."

Bronnya hit the same crest behind her, cackling so hard that Jallen shouted her name. The tanker landed with a tremendous splash, bent low over her board, then straightened to howl her delight across the beach.
"Again! Handsome guy, another one!!"
Quinlan obliged. Jallen took the new swell alongside her captain, smiling into the wind while Bronnya demanded that they try the bigger wave behind it too.
The Lilies carried on, shouting over each other, and Lilith's laughter reached all the way back to the sand.
On the beach, the remaining lords and the Obsidian Circle watched Quinlan send Synchra up a steep swell with his daughter on his shoulders.
"Higher!!"
He obliged, and his wives raced after him into the curling water, their wedding dresses flashing white against the blue.

Ayame cut across the crest with her skirt gathered in one hand, giggling as Serika rode up beneath her. The brawler kicked her board around at the top and dropped backward down the wave, red hair flying.
"They came straight from their wedding," Maelstrom muttered.
"We were there," Brokk reminded him.
"Look at them!"

The women raced through the spray on either side of their husband, silk flaring around powerful legs. Quinlan laughed and raised another wave for his wives, his little girl shrieking her approval above his head.
They were magnificent. Iskaris's new ruling family was riding the ocean in its wedding finery, enjoying the freedom they earned.
Gorruk gave a deep, amused rumble.
"If our fate was to be conquered, we could have ended up with a much worse tyrant."

chapters.title: Chapter 1948 Battling Underwater
paragraphs: "Aye," Brokk admitted, her hands resting in her belt as she watched them.

The thought brought some comfort to those remaining on the sand. They had entrusted their peoples to this man, and he was spending the afternoon sharing his impossible new freedom with their families.
"Aunt Lilith, not fair!!" Felicity was jumping beside her father. "Dad! We have to go too!"
"I heard you the first time, Felicity. Give me a moment to take my boots off."
"Feng! He said yes!!"
"Only little girls wait for their dads!" Feng had picked up a board.
"Rude!!" Felicity shrieked, rushing after the oriental girl from another world.
Alexios left his boots and coat on the sand, then followed the girls into the water with a board under his arm.
Felicity climbed onto Feng's board and grabbed her shoulders. Feng used her Tidebreaker magic to redirect the incoming current beneath the wood, nudging its nose toward the next wave.
"Left! Let's go left!"
"Then stop leaning right! Wait, why are you on my board to begin with?"
"Why not? Hehe!"

Quinlan eased them onto a gentle wave, and Alexios followed on his own board. The old geezer seemed to have gotten into the mood, for Quinlan knew he normally never would've partaken in such a silly act.
But bringing down the Heavenly Restriction? For a man who spent a millennium under its oppression?
It deserved a proper celebration.
'What a cool dad.' Quinlan grinned inwardly, fully approving.
"Father!" Kitsara called to Vargis. "Don't let the other dads outshine you."
"Yes, darling..." Vargis sighed tiredly, resigned to his fate of wet fur. "I'm coming."
Vargis carried a board down to Kitsara, who clasped his hand as he stepped aboard. Rosie grew a broader one for Gorruk from the roots in the sand, and the other lords followed them into the surf.
When the bearkin got moving, Skarn and Rajah were racing.
Brokk left her formal coat beside Alexios's boots and joined them with the Obsidian Circle. Maelstrom lingered in the shallows to help the Mediator onto his board.
"Just hold it still," the old man said, gripping the general's shoulder. "For a moment, just..."
Quinlan steadied the wood with his magic. The Mediator got his feet under him, stared down at the water passing beneath the board, and began to laugh through the tears in his beard.
Myrasyn chose a board and waded out after the others, holding her white dress above the water. She stepped onto it just as Black Fang sped past her on a rising wave.
"Wait for me!"
The Venomborne Terror glanced back at her friend. Myrasyn leaned forward to follow, her ears lifting as her board picked up speed.
"Oh! I think I've-"
Its nose dug into the next swell, and the governor pitched headfirst into the sea.
"Kyaa!"
*Splash!*
Myrasyn surfaced with wet strands plastered across her face, blinking away seawater. "I spent my entire morning on my hair..."

Quinlan smirked as he drew the water from Myrasyn's dress, then from her dripping strands. She gave him a mortified look before climbing back onto her board, determined to follow Black Fang on her next attempt.
His submerged net tugged for his attention, reporting movement along its outer curtain. Quinlan checked each disturbance, then sent the next swell toward the people calling his name.
"Papa! Everybody's coming!"
Rosie was ecstatic.
Quinlan peered up at his daughter. Rosie hugged his head and cheered for her mommies, oblivious to her father's gaze.
He held her legs closer and allowed himself to enjoy what they had done for these people.
Quinlan felt his outer curtain bend around a long, heavy body approaching from below the shelf.
He faced the disturbance at once. The inner curtain remained undisturbed, and he guided the waves beneath the surfers back toward the shallows before the creature could reach them.
"Something's rising from deeper water," he called. "Stay nearer the beach while I take a look."
"Daddy, Rosie will-"
"-take a break." Quinlan finished the sentence for her, taking the girl off his shoulders, then flinging her toward the shore with a gust of wind.
"Eh?"
His daughter had the look of utter betrayal.
"Ehhhhh???"
She folded her arms and crossed her legs in midair, pouting furiously at him as she sailed over the waves.
Rosie grew a thick branch from the sand and curled its leafy tip beneath herself. It bowed under her landing, then lifted her into a seat overlooking the water.
"Hmph!"
Ayame was already turning toward the others. <We'll keep them here.>
But Black Fang was heading in the opposite direction of the shore, listening with her head angled toward the deeper water.
Quinlan eased his board beside hers and peered down. The pale seabed ended below them, dropping into blue, and a huge serpent was rising along the drop.

He pressed a current against its flank, turning it away from the swimming area. The beast fought the pull, its body bending around the resistance, and Quinlan increased the pressure until he could force it back below the shelf.

It was strong, incredibly so, but not enough to overpower Quinlan. He felt the force of its muscles against his magic as it twisted free, then searched the neighboring water for anything following behind it.
The serpent was alone.
When Quinlan looked back at Black Fang, she was regarding him with a hunger he knew very well.
She wanted to kill it.
Quinlan checked the currents between the serpent and his family once more. Then he grinned at her.
"Let's do this."
Black Fang was already in action. She filled her lungs and dived off her board.
He drove a current after her, catching her straightened body and sending her hurtling down through the water with a trail of white bubbles behind her.
"Oh no, Master is going full psycho mode." Vex shook her head.
"It was bound to happen," Ayame sighed. "I'm honestly shocked she held back until now."
Synchra flowed up Quinlan's legs as he stepped off her board form. Her plates smoothed against his body, sealing at the joints until the sea slid over an unbroken black surface.
Quinlan used his wind magic to pack fresh air around his head.
The helmet closed over the trapped air, and he dived. Synchra flattened the ridges along his limbs as he accelerated, letting him cut through the water with his arms held close.
He caught the Soul Reaper as it dived after him and sent a current down his back to catch up with Black Fang.
Quinlan reached Black Fang as she unsheathed her serpent-patterned blade. Dark venom welled along its edge, shedding black threads into the sea.
He curled a narrow current around the steel, holding her leaking poison against the blade as she aimed it at the serpent's eye.

The beast rose to meet them, blue-black plates grinding together along a body longer than a river barge. Jagged spines lined its back, and its open mouth was big enough to swallow either of them whole.
"Sashimi time." Quinlan grinned inside his helmet.
Black Fang lunged. He swept toward the opposite side of its head with the Soul Reaper held high, driving water against its flank to angle it toward her.
The creature's gills flared, releasing a pressure wave.
*BOOM!*
The pressure hit Quinlan hard enough to crush the breath out of him. Synchra braced his ribs as he tumbled backward, pain ringing through his chest beneath the sealed plate.
"Ngh!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1949 A Shocking Number
paragraphs: Black Fang's blade skidded across an armored scale. The serpent lunged at her before she could recover, and the water dragged against her twisting body.
Her first underwater fight was giving her few chances to learn.
Quinlan seized the seawater around his shoulders with his magic and stopped his tumble. His muscles swelled as he hauled his knees toward his chest, pushing Synchra's thigh plates outward.
He packed the sea behind his boots into a foothold, and Synchra braced his spine, crimson seams blazing as he planted his feet against it.

He kicked hard enough to blow the compressed water apart. Bubbles erupted behind his heels as Quinlan hurtled back toward the serpent, his magic forcing a path through the sea until its gill was within sword reach.
Quinlan pushed against Black Fang's hip with a current, carrying her through the turn. As its teeth snapped shut behind her, he thrust the Soul Reaper into the gill the monster had exposed to him.
The saber bit through cartilage. Quinlan shoved it deeper, then ripped it toward himself, opening the creature's neck in a gush of blood.
"GRRROOOO!!"
Black Fang was returning. She planted a foot against its cheek and buried her poisoned blade beneath the plate above his cut.
The exposed flesh blackened around her steel. As the venom spread, the serpent shuddered violently as it tried to twist around, its muscles seizing along that side of its neck.
Quinlan swept the poisoned blood away from their bodies with a current aimed toward deeper water. He maintained the flow as he pulled the Soul Reaper free for another strike.
Black Fang bared her teeth at him and kicked off the beast to give him room.

Quinlan pressurized a narrow stream of seawater and fired it through the wound she'd opened. Scales erupted outward as the jet peeled the damaged plate from its neck, cutting deep into the flesh beneath.
The serpent whipped its tail toward him.
He hauled a wall of water into its path.
*BOOM!*
The collision buckled his barrier and hurled him backward. Synchra tightened around his ribs as the shock tore through his chest, the rocky shelf rushing closer behind him.

Quinlan seized the seawater against his back and pushed forward with it. The opposing force stopped his retreat, but the monster kept bearing down on his barrier, its tail grinding through the churning water.
"Ngh!"

He could feel the strength in that enormous body through every current it displaced. The creature was trying to crush him with the same water he commanded, and Quinlan bared his teeth inside his helmet.
He wanted to beat it at that.

Quinlan dragged more of the surrounding sea into his barrier, packing the flow against its tail until the armored length stopped advancing. Sand ripped off the seabed in streaming clouds as the water rushed past him.
The serpent strained against him, its coils knotting as it fought for another inch. Quinlan laughed into his helmet and increased the pressure until he began forcing it back.
Black Fang slipped beneath its head while it struggled against him. Her sword opened the flesh beside its gills, and the monster jerked toward her with its mouth spreading wide.
Quinlan reversed the current along its flank.

The water the serpent had pushed against to turn now threw its head in the opposite direction. Its teeth snapped shut on empty sea while Black Fang swept past its throat, her blade carving another bloody line.
"GRRRAAA!!"
The beast lashed its tail to dive after her. Quinlan hauled the water beneath its belly upward, rolling the huge body sideways over the shelf before it could descend.
He clamped opposing currents around its midsection, holding it over the shelf. While it fought the pressure pinning it there, his earth magic thrust a stone spike up through its exposed underside.
Its whole body convulsed.
Quinlan pulled himself aside with water magic while Black Fang slipped along the trapped coil. Her blade opened its belly as she passed, her skirt catching on a spine and tearing along her thigh.
"GRRRAAA!!"
Blackened blood poured after her. Quinlan dragged it down toward the seabed, keeping the water around her clear while he thrust the Soul Reaper through another gap in the armor.
His outer warning curtain tugged at his attention. He read the harmless fish passing through it and kept the boundary in place, his saber buried in the thrashing monster.

The serpent wrenched against Quinlan's currents until the flesh around the stone spike tore, leaving a chunk of its body behind. Its head swung toward Black Fang, jaws spreading while its surviving gill swelled for another blast.
She met Quinlan's gaze, then eyed the corner of that open mouth. She tucked her knees beneath her, ready to push off the water he was gathering behind her feet.
He wrenched the Soul Reaper free and surged toward the other side of its head.
*BOOM!*

Quinlan split the pressure wave around Black Fang with his water magic and launched her through the opening. At the same time, he forced a jet into the serpent's torn gill and froze it inside the wound.
Ice ruptured its cheek, levering the mouth wider just as she reached it.
Black Fang caught the corner of its mouth and swung herself against its face. She drove her blade through the roof of its mouth while Quinlan rammed his saber through the breach in its cheek.
Both weapons punched into its skull.
The monster tried to bite down, scraping Black Fang's forearm with its teeth. Quinlan forced its lower jaw away with a current as she planted her foot against it and tore her sword sideways.
He ripped the Soul Reaper in the opposite direction.
*CRUNCH!*
The head came apart between them. Broken fangs spun through the water with fragments of bone, and blood engulfed both killers as the enormous body thrashed through its final convulsions.
Quinlan trapped the tail with his water magic and shoved it down toward the seabed. He was laughing inside his helmet when Black Fang emerged from the red cloud, her blade still in her hand.
She looked at him with savage delight, black silk fluttering around her bare thigh.
Quinlan grinned back, exhilarated by their kill. She had committed to each dangerous opening with complete confidence that he would get her through it.
Seeing that they were becoming quite the synergistic duo made him smile from ear to ear, two proper psychos staring at each other deep underwater.
He swept the blood and venom away from them in an outward current, then caught the dead serpent in a separate flow before it could sink.
Quinlan pulled the carcass after him, already looking forward to bringing his wives a ridiculous amount of sashimi.
A window flashed across Black Fang's vision.
Black Fang stared at the notification, her sword lowering until it hung beside her leg.
Quinlan's own reward appeared in his vision. He left it unread, watching her. He was eager to see the expression this woman made after seeing a bigger number than one after such a long wait.
Instead she remained suspended in the water, so absorbed in the window that even the blood drifting past her face went ignored.
Concern drew him to her. He washed the blood away with a current and gathered her into his arms, one beneath her knees, the other supporting her back.
She let him, still staring ahead.
He drove a rising column of water beneath them and took her straight to the surface.
A separate current towed the serpent's carcass up after them, keeping it away from their bodies as they rose.
Black Fang drew in a deep breath as they broke through. Synchra's helmet flowed away from Quinlan's face while he steadied the water beneath his feet, holding her above the swell.
"Are you alright?"
"...One million two hundred thousand."
Quinlan's eyes widened.
So much XP for a monster below their level?

chapters.title: Chapter 1950 Too Much XP
paragraphs: Quinlan studied Black Fang, then the dead serpent floating beside them, held at the surface by his water magic.
"One million two hundred thousand XP? From that?"
"Yes."
She remained in his arms, violet eyes fixed on her notification. Water dripped from the ends of her black strands onto Synchra's armor.
The monster had been level seventy. Even sharing the kill with him, she had received a reward that left him eager to dive down there and find another immediately.

Quinlan formed a screen of water between them and the beach. Black Fang's torn and drenched skirt had fallen open over his supporting arm. The people on the shore had already enjoyed quite enough of a spectacle today.
Wet silk clung to her waist, following every curve before gathering beneath his palm at her back. Her bare thigh rested against his wrist, droplets sliding down the pale skin to fall into the sea.
Quinlan glanced at her and found her watching him now.
She had sheathed her sword and apparently wasn't in a rush to land on her feet.
"Your thoughts?"
"That today is one amazing day."
"On the reward."
"Ah. Those thoughts."
Her stare remained utterly flat. Quinlan answered it by giving her thigh a squeeze, his smile entirely unapologetic.
'Quinlan Elysiar. Enough simping already.'
He eased his arm farther beneath her knees before glancing toward their kill.
Then Quinlan brought up the reward notification he had ignored underwater.
"Oh."
His share was even larger than hers. He checked the figure against his status, already imagining what a day of hunting out here could earn them.
The reward was a welcome addition to his XP, though he was still far from filling that enormous bar.
"One million eight hundred thousand. I got more than you did."
Black Fang studied his face.
"You were five levels below it."
"That probably helped. As for why we both got so much..."
He glanced toward the floating serpent.
"It could be the fight itself. We were underwater for the first time, lacking oxygen, fighting it on its home turf where we were greatly disadvantaged."
Black Fang listened without shifting against him. A wet strand lay across her cheek, and Quinlan lifted it away with a curl of air.
"I helped you move, but it was still an extremely dangerous place to fight. Perhaps we were rewarded for that."
"Perhaps."
She sounded unconvinced. Quinlan could hardly blame her.
"Or the serpent was unusual. For all we know, we just killed some rare monster people spend years looking for."
Black Fang regarded the huge carcass beyond his shoulder. Its ruined skull bobbed in the current he was using to keep it afloat.
"It died easily enough."
"With the two of us splitting its skull."
"Yes."
Quinlan chuckled. The shallow wound on her forearm was still bleeding, and she was dismissing the creature that had put it there.
He washed the cut with clean water, then kept a gentle pressure over it while she considered his suggestions.
"I'm not claiming either explanation is right," he added. "Just making some guesses."
Her eyes returned to his.
"We need a larger sample."
The Venomborne Terror spoke with complete composure, reclining against him while proposing they slaughter more of the outside world.
Quinlan grinned down at her.
"Yeah. Only one way to solve this mystery. We'll have to gather more evidence."
Black Fang nodded to him, then looked past him toward the horizon, her violet gaze searching the water. Quinlan felt his own eagerness rising as he followed it. They had barely left the beach.
Quinlan carried Black Fang back toward the surfers on a moving column of water, towing their kill in a separate current behind him.
Once they crossed his inner warning curtain, he called his wives through [Master's Link]. <We're done. Everyone alright?>
<Everyone except a certain little lady, who is filing a complaint,> Ayame replied. <Quin, why are you carrying my sister?>
<Why not?>
<Opportunistic as always, I see~> Lucille purred.
Ayame rode her board out to meet them, her concern easing when she saw Black Fang's face. Quinlan drew the water from the assassin's clothes before lowering the screen around them.
"Big sis, did you forget how to walk?"
"We're in the ocean."
Ayame eyed Quinlan's hold pointedly.

The samurai understood very well that the Venomborne Terror couldn't walk on the water, but still. Never in a thousand years would Black Fang let a man princess carry her, a man visibly enjoying his hold on her thigh.
If he were anyone else, he'd have already lost his life and she'd just swim out to shore. With her speed and power, it wouldn't take more than a few moves.
Her sister ignored her narrowed gaze, waiting until he brought them into the shallows before putting her feet down.
A rush of Quinlan's water magic swept the serpent up the beach. Quinlan lowered its body onto the wet sand, where it lay long enough to make the nearest boards look like toys.
"You brought that back?!" Ayame stared at its broken skull.
"I thought we could have a special lunch. It's still our wedding day, after all."
She inspected the blackened wounds running along its body.
"You want to feed your newlywed wives with poisoned monster meat."
Her tone sounded rather dry.
Aurora joined Ayame, studying the pale flesh farther down the serpent's body. The alchemist traced the spreading discoloration back toward the wounds Black Fang had inflicted.
"Could you draw the poison out? I can check the meat as you work. We should discard everything it's already ruined."
Black Fang crouched beside the carcass.
To Quinlan's surprise, the Venomborne Terror seemed uncharacteristically interested in tasting her first kill outside the barrier.
He grew a broad slab of stone beneath their catch to keep it clear of the sand. Synchra flowed out of her armor plates into a black shirt and trousers as he joined the women beside it.
Aurora retrieved her testing kit from storage. At her request, Quinlan accessed [Slave Monitor] and switched her active class to Alchemist before she began.
Black Fang pressed her fingers beside an exposed stretch of muscle and cast a spell to draw out the poison.
At her pull, dark droplets welled out of the flesh and gathered above the wound. Aurora held a glass vial beneath them, and Black Fang guided the poison inside before moving farther along the flank.

The unexpected duo worked together to cleanse its flesh. As Aurora pointed out the portions that remained discolored, Black Fang cut them away with her sword and pushed them to the far end of the slab.
By the time Aurora was satisfied, the ruined meat lay apart from the clean portions. The alchemist stoppered the vial of recovered poison and put it away.
"Now we can eat it," Aurora announced.
"Music to my ears." Quinlan floated a long strip of meat off the stone with his wind magic. "Ayame, would you help with the slicing?"
"Naturally. We can't trust you to do it right~"

Ayame unsheathed her katana while Black Fang separated the remaining flesh from the bones. Black Fang passed Ayame a clean length, and the Skysplitter's blade swept through it in a series of gleaming cuts.
*Shik! Shik! Shik!*
Thin slices fell onto the smooth stone Quinlan conjured beside her. He cooled the slab with his ice magic while the sisters worked through another portion.
"Like that?" Ayame asked, balancing a slice on the flat of her blade.
Quinlan leaned forward and took it between his teeth.
"Mm. Perfect."
"Of course it is."
For the rest, he had a different plan.
Quinlan thrust a stone skewer up from the sand with his earth magic, its rising point making the nearest onlookers step back.
Using his wind magic, he threaded the thick cuts onto it before lowering both ends into supports he grew beneath them.
"That's a spit?" Brokk demanded, studying its enormous length.
"We have a bear to feed."
Gorruk gave an approving rumble.
Quinlan sent fire rolling beneath the meat. Flames climbed above him, washing the pale flesh gold while a current of air rotated the skewer in its supports.
Fat dripped into the blaze with a loud hiss. He raised the flames beneath the thickest cuts, letting the smaller pieces brown over gentler heat.
"Oh, that smells wonderful," Lucille sighed, coming to stand beside him.
"Want to try the first bite?"
"Very much." She opened her mouth, expectant.
Quinlan shaved a morsel from the browned surface with a thin blade of wind. He cooled it with a gentle current of air before bringing it to her lips.
"Mmm~" Lucille closed her lips around the offered bite, smiling at him as she chewed.

While the monster cooked, the girls brought out seasonings and plates from their supplies. Ayame's sashimi circulated through the gathering, and Quinlan shaped benches from the sand so their guests could sit.
The beastkin lords hesitated beside the new seats. The Obsidian Circle lingered farther back with unused plates while his family crowded around the roast.

They were being offered lunch by their conqueror, with his brides arguing over which part of the monster looked tastiest. Maelstrom glanced toward the Mediator, who seemed equally uncertain where to sit.
"There's room here," Lucille offered, moving a plate along the bench. "Would you care for some of the raw slices while we wait?"
"...Thank you."
The Mediator lowered himself onto the seat. Maelstrom joined him after another glance at the fire, and the beastkin began finding places nearby.
Gorruk tried a slice, considered it, then reached for another. Brokk chose to wait for the roast, watching Quinlan regulate the heat with her thumbs hooked in her belt.
When the first cuts were ready, Quinlan pulled them off the spit with his wind magic. Ayame carved off steaming portions while he held the meat above the plates his wives extended toward her.
"Careful, it's hot," Jasmine warned, then took a bite of her own and promptly had to blow through her mouth.
Quinlan laughed. "Good?"
